TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. T2 hyperintense signal at the medial femoral condyle, consistent with osseous contusion. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Low-grade chondral lesion in the distal femoral diaphysis.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the posterior horn without extrusion. No flipped fragments. No parameniscal cyst.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Oblique tear of the posterior horn without extrusion. No flipped fragments. Parameniscal cyst adjacent to the body measuring 1.1 x 1.6 cm.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Increased signal in the proximal fibular collateral ligament, consistent with prior injury. No tear.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Globular T1 hyperintense and T2 hyperintense lesion within the superolateral Hoffa's fat pad measuring 1.2 x 2.1 x 2.5 cm. The lesion abuts the cartilage surface of the patella and lateral trochlea.
Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Globular T2 hyperintense lesion within the superolateral Hoffa's fat measuring 2.5 cm. Differential diagnosis includes fat pad impingement, localized nodular synovitis, amongst other etiologies. Biopsy is recommended.
2.	Osseous contusion of the anterior medial femoral condyle.
3.	Oblique tear of the lateral meniscus posterior horn without extrusion.
4.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus posterior horn without effusion.

Keine Herniation. Geringe Extrusionsstellung des Innenmeniskus.  
Umgebende Weichteile: 
Unauffällig, keine muskuläre Atrophie.

Small joint effusion. Mild, diffuse synovial proliferation. No loose intra-articular bodies are seen. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild quadriceps tendinosis.

Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Large, complex tear of the medial meniscus.

2. Chondrosis in the medial tibiofemoral compartment.

3. Quadriceps and patellar tendinosis with interstitial tearing at the distal patellar tendon.

4. Small joint effusion. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

COMPARISON:Prior imaging in back to [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Progressive right knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Inferiorly surfacing oblique tear posterior horn medial meniscus extending into the body, which is peripherally extruded. There is a superimposed complex tear of the posterior root. The anterior horn is intact.

Complex tear posterior root and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with peripheral extrusion of the lateral meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without intervertebral translation. There is a low-grade partial-thickness tear of the posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Severe popliteus tendinosis without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. Moderate pretibial superficial bursitis.

There is generalized thinning of patellofemoral articular cartilage with focal full thickness cartilage denuding along the lateral patellar facet near the patellar apex. There is thinning of lateral femorotibial articular cartilage. There is thinning of medial femorotibial articular cartilage.

Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex medial meniscal tear with medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Complex lateral meniscal tear with lateral meniscal extrusion.
3. Chronic complete anterior cruciate ligament tear without tibial translation.
4. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the posterior cruciate ligament.
5. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
6. Moderate tricompartment chondrosis consistent with moderate tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.

original_report: МР находка: МР данни за ставен излив. Костите, формиращи дясната колянна става се изобразяват с правилна форма, структура и сигнална характеристика. МР данни за костномозъчен едем в долната медиална половина на пателата. Вижда се малък дефект в хрущяла на пателата с микрокистична преустройка на нивото на дефекта по горния полюс на пателата на медиалната страна.  Хрущялът, покриващ ставните повърхности на тибията и фемура е с нормална дебелина, хомогенна структура и сигнален интензитет. Установяват се дегенеративни изменения в задния рог на медиалния менискус под формата на тънка хиперинтензна линия с хоризонтален ход.  Латерален мениск - нормално изобразяване. Предната кръстна връзка е със запазена цялост и се изобразява с повишен сигнален интензитет и лекостепенно задебелена, както при разтежение.  Задната кръстна връзка и двата колатерални лигамента се проследяват до залавните си места с правилна форма, хомогенна структура и сигнален интензитет. Пателарен лигамент и двата ретинакулума са с нормално представяне. От двете страни по хода на латералния ретинакулум се вижда течност, с незначителен едем на меките тъкани по съседство. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – б.о. Фоса поплитеа – б.о. Заключение:  МР данни за малък ставен излив. Дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус и предната кръстна връзка. Дефект в хрущяла на пателата в горния полюс, с наличие на костномозъчен едем в долния медиален ръб.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Six-week history of knee pain associated with hockey localized to the anterior knee. No prior surgery.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Mild to moderate osteoarthritis of the proximal tibiofibular joint characterized by marginal osteophyte formation, chondrosis and mild subchondral bone marrow edema.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. There is a new 1.1 cm ossified intra-articular body localized posterior to the PCL (series 4, image 12). No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss about the central and posterior weightbearing medial femoral condyle with superimposed areas of full-thickness fissuring and mild subchondral marrow edema, progressed from prior.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness fissuring involving the median ridge and lateral patellar facet with mild subchondral marrow edema and cystic change, low-grade partial-thickness loss along the medial patellar facet peripherally. Focal full-thickness fissuring involving the mid to inferior lateral femoral trochlea with mild subchondral marrow edema superimposed on diffuse high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the lateral femoral trochlea. [REDACTED].

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Moderate prepatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Progressive patellofemoral greater than medial tibiofemoral compartment chondrosis.
2.	Small joint effusion with new 1.1 cm ossified intra-articular body posterior to the PCL.
3.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis without tear.
4.	Moderate prepatellar bursitis.

Findings:  Small knee joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Large multiloculated ganglion cyst possibly originating from the lateral head of gastrocnemius tendon origin, and extending posterosuperiorly into the surrounding soft tissues extending from the origin of the lateral head of gastrocnemius  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments. Radial tear of the anterior horn/body junction of the medial meniscus with partial extrusion of the body from the joint space. Intact lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band, popliteus tendon and pes anserine tendons.  Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons.  Severe patellofemoral degenerative change with diffuse full-thickness chondral loss along the retropatellar facets and corresponding femoral trochlea, and chronic underlying bone stress changes together with attrition/moulding of the retropatellar facets.  Full-thickness chondral loss is also appreciated in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle. Low-grade chondral thinning in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Scattered intraosseous ganglion cyst noted in both the distal femur and proximal tibia. Tricompartmental marginal osteophyte formation also noted.  
Conclusion:  Radial tear of the body of the medial meniscus. Severe patellofemoral and to a lesser extent medial tibiofemoral compartment degenerative changes. Ancillary findings described above.

Lateral menisküs normal. Medyal menisküs gövdesi düzeyindeki dejenerasyona arka boynuzu/gövdesi bileşkesindeki milimetrik radyal yırtık eşlik ediyor. Diz ekleminin posteromedyali ödemli olup posterior oblik-oblik popliteyal bağlardaki kalınlaşma ve intensite artışı ile birlikte. Kuadriseps yağ yastıkçığındaki hafif dereceli ödem ön diz ağrısı nedeni olabilir. Kemiklerdeki subkortikal milimetrik boyutlu T2 intensite artışları osteopeniyi telkin ediyor. Kemiklerin medülla intensiteleri bunların dışında normal. İç yan bağın çevresi ödemli. Dış yan bağ, çapraz bağlar normal. Diz eklemi çevresindeki kas yapılar atrofik. Изобразяват се масивни остеофитни наслоявания по кондилите на фемура и тибията от латералната страна на колянната става. Изострени интеркондиларни еминенции. Артикулиращият хрущял на фемура и тибията е с нарушена конгруентност до липсващ от латералната страна. МР данни за парциална руптура на предната кръстна връзка с давност (в горна трета връзката е изтънена и се представя с повишен интензитет на сигнала). Нормално представена задна кръстна връзка.

Предният рог на последният не се изобразява на топичното си място, а е изместен над еминенциите , като е налице патогномоничния double PCL sign. Задният рог е руптуриран с увреда  2а степен. Дегенеративни промени в медиалния менискус. Колатерални лигаменти - със запазена цялост. Патела – малки кисти субкортикално по задна стена,  хрущял на пателата - липсва ретинакулуми – б.о. Визуализира се малка многокамерна Бекерова киста на нивото на медиалната глава на м. гастрокнемиус с коронарен р-р 18/11мм. Лимфедем в меките тъкани на коляното. Заключение:  МР данни за тежки гонартрозни промени на дясната колянна става . Хондропатия. МР данни за частична руптура с давност на предна кръстна връзка. MRI of Left Knee with 
-SG PD FatSat, Locator, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* Shallow trochlear groove with supratrochlear spur and lateral displacement of patella, indicative of trochlear dysplasia with suspicious of lateral patellar tilting.
   Increased signal intensity of the medial and lateral patellar retinaculum with surrounding soft tissue edema, in favor of grade 2 injury.
   Bone marrow edema over medial aspect of patella and lateral aspect of lateral femoral condyle, R/O bone contusion.
* Wearing of the articular cartilage of patellofemoral joint and spur formation of patella, femur and anterior tibial plateau with subchondral bone marrow edema, reflecting osteoarthritis; subchondral cystic change over tibial plateau.
* There is linear signal intensity in anterior horn of lateral meniscus and posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extends into the surface, R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal, maybe due to degeneration.
* High signal intensity in the soft tissues around the medial and lateral collateral ligaments and ACL, in favor of grade 1 injury.
* Joint effusion with suprapatellar expension and hypertrophy of the synovium; suprapatellar, medial and lateral plicae can also be noted, indicative of synovitis.
* Subcutaneous edema around left knee; increased fat stranding over infrapatellar fat pad.
* Mild muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
> The contour of PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of tear is noted in  lateral meniscus in this study.
> The quadriceps and patellar tendons appear to be within normal.

Impression:
1. Transient patellar dislocation with tear of medial patellar retinaculum near patellar attachment and bone contusion of medial aspect of patella and lateral femoral condyle.
2. Trochlear dysplasia with shallow femoral trochlear groove and in favor of lateral patellar tilting in this study.
3. Grade 1 injury of ACL, MCL and  LCL.
4. Subcutaneous and interstitial edema around left knee and muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
5. Osteoarthritis of left knee with synovitis and patellar plicae.
6. R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal in anterior horn of lateral meniscus and posterior horn of medial meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

Il n’y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire ni kyste de Baker significatif avec un liséré de liquide.

Il y a un émoussement vertical à la périphérie de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne, de signal moindre par rapport au liquide, qui pourrait être en lien avec une ancienne déchirure longitudinale verticale à la jonction capsulo-méniscale/lésion de type « ramp ». Cette formation kystique pourrait être en lien avec un kyste paraméniscal dans ce contexte ou un kyste paraganglionnaire.

Il y a une légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémorotibial interne, sans atteinte transfixiante ni changement sous-chondral réactionnel associé, à l'exception d'un minime œdème sous-chondral au versant tibial.

Le ménisque externe et le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts et sans déchirure.

Les surfaces cartilagineuses fémorotibiales externes sont relativement préservées. 

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts et sans déchirure. 

L’alignement patellofémoral demeure dans les limites de la normale. Il y a un foyer d’œdème au sein de la graisse de Hoffa supéro-externe suggérant un syndrome d’accrochage entre le tendon patellaire et le condyle fémoral externe (« Hoffa fat pad impingement »). Il y a une légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces chondrales au compartiment patellofémoral, sans atteinte transfixiante. 

Il y a un petit enthésophyte à l’insertion distale du tendon du quadriceps avec un minime œdème réactionnel associé. Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts et sans déchirure. Il n'y a pas de bursite prérotulienne ni infrapatellaire significative notée.

Conclusion :

Il y a un léger émoussement vertical à la périphérie de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne qui pourrait être en lien avec une ancienne déchirure longitudinale verticale à la jonction capsulo-méniscale/lésion de type « ramp. » Il y a une formation kystique multilobulée postéro-interne en lien soit avec un kyste paraméniscal dans ce contexte ou un kyste ganglionnaire.

Il y a un léger œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa suggérant un accrochage entre le tendon patellaire et le condyle fémoral externe (« Hoffa fat pad impingement »). Ceci pourrait être une cause de douleur périrotulienne. Il y a un léger enthésophyte à l’insertion distale du tendon du quadriceps sans déchirure. 

Il y a une légère chondropathie patellofémorale et fémorotibiale interne.

Il n'y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. 

Il n'y a pas de fracture.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patella demonstrates severe chondral fraying with some regions of focal cartilage loss seen to the lateral facet and apex of the patella. These changes are associated with subcortical cyst formation and edema seen to the patella involving lateral facet and apex.
The articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea is reasonably well-maintained apart from mild fissuring seen at the medial femoral trochlear articular surface.

The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is reasonably well-maintained with only mild chondral fraying.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small ganglion cyst projecting posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 1.4 x 0.9 x 0.6 cm. Centrally within this ganglion cyst there is a small loose body measuring 6 mm.

No significant knee effusion is detected. No significant Baker's cyst.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe chondrosis and involving the patellofemoral joint.

Mild patellar tendinosis. Associated prepatellar bursitis.

Mild chondrosis to the medial joint compartment.

Small ganglion cyst behind the posterior cruciate ligament with small loose body.

ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ - Αναγνωρίζεται παθολογικό σήμα και ασυνέχεια του πρόσθιου χιαστού συνδέσμου - Ασυνέχεια αντίστοιχα με την μηριαία πρόσφυση ελέγχεται στον οπίσθιο χιαστό σύνδεσμο. - Οίδημα οστικού μυελού αναγνωρίζεται αντίστοιχα με την πρόσθια μοίρα του έσω μηριαίου και οπίσθια μοίρα του έσω κνημιαίου κονδύλου.  - Παρατηρείται γραμμοειδές παθολογικό σήμα στο σώμα και οπίσθιο κέρας του έσω μηνίσκου. Παθολογικό σήμα αναγνωρίζεται και στο οπίσθιο κέρας του έξω μηνίσκου, ενώ μηνισκικό τεμάχιο ελέγχεται παρεκτοπισμένο στη μεσοκονδύλια εντομή. - Ακέραιος ελέγχεται ο έσω πλάγιος σύνδεσμος ενώ ο έξω πλάγιος αναγνωρίζεται με παθολογικό σήμα και κυματοειδή μορφολογία. - Ο ιγνυοπερονικός σύνδεσμος δεν αναγνωρίζεται. - Παθολογικό σήμα αναγνωρίζεται αντίστοιχα με την κατάφυση του ιγνυακού τένοντα. - Παρατηρείται παθολογικό σήμα στην άπω μοίρα του έσω και έξω πλατέος μυός καθώς και στις γαστέρες του γαστροκνημίου. - Αναγνωρίζεται μεγάλη ενδαρθρική συλλογή υγρού ανομοιογενούς έντασης σήματος, ως επί αίμαρθρου. - Δεν παρατηρούνται άξια λόγου ευρήματα από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού μηχανισμού. - Οιδηματώδης απεικόνιση των μαλακών μορίων πέριξ του γόνατος. MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  [Age] ongoing lists knee pain with minimal imaging findings on x-ray and ultrasound. The radiologist recommend arranging MRI to further investigate.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Background of intrasubstance degeneration of the medial and lateral meniscus. 

Complex undersurface tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with the formation 2 mm the parameniscal cyst (401:109). In addition, there is a horizontal cleavage tear extending through the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus extending into the lateral meniscal body. No lateral meniscal extrusion.

Inferiorly surfacing oblique tear posterior horn of the medial meniscus with 4 mm parameniscal cyst (401:194). There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament.

PCL, MCL and LCL are intact.

Insertional tendinosis of the popliteus tendon.

Scattered area of high-grade chondrosis with full-thickness cartilage loss noted along the patellar surface of the patellofemoral compartment, on a background of generalized cartilage thinning. There is also generalized thinning of lateral femorotibial articular cartilage foci of full-thickness cartilage denuding involving the posterior nonweightbearing aspect lateral femoral condyle and the central weightbearing aspect lateral tibial plateau. Within the medial femorotibial compartment, is moderate chondrosis.

Trace volume joint effusion.

Scattered subcutaneous edema more pronounced along the anterior aspect the knee.

The extensor mechanism, quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Scattered subcentimeter cysts at the popliteal fossa.

INTERPRETATION:

Complex tear posterior horn lateral meniscus with additional horizontal cleavage tear involving the body and anterior horn. Parameniscal cyst formation as described. No lateral meniscal extrusion.

Inferiorly subtle tear posterior horn medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion and parameniscal cyst formation as described.

Tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral and lateral femorotibial compartments. Findings are in keeping with moderate OA.

MRI RIGHT KNEE

Clinical information: [Age]. Ongoing medial meniscus pain with mechanical symptoms and swelling.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the right knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Comparison examination: Previous radiographs of bilateral knees from [Date].

FINDINGS:
There is a radial tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus measuring 0.8 cm. There are extensive degenerative changes of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with extensive apical fraying. There is a focal oblique tear involving the posterior horn and posterior aspect of the body of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface.

There is a chronic tearing of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is a T2 hyperintensity within the midportion of the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 0.4 x 0.3 cm representing a small intraligamentous ganglion.

There is mild thickening of the proximal medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a focal severe chondrosis involving the weightbearing zone and posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle with focal deep cartilage defect and small adjacent cystic changes. There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a mild superficial chondral disease involving the patellofemoral joint. There are focal small osteophytes at the inner aspect of the intercondylar notch

There is a mild anterior tibial translation [9 mm]. The no acute bony contusions. There is a mild joint effusion with reactive synovial thickening. There are multiple intra-articular bodies, for example posterior to the distal attachment of the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 0.6 x 0.4 cm. There is a large (2.0 x 0.8 cm), well-corticated bone fragment adjacent to the posterolateral aspect of the tibial plateau, representing another intra-articular body.

There is a low volume Baker's cyst. Small cluster of cysts in the popliteal fossa measuring a maximum of 10 mm AP by 20 mm transverse radiology a of a of alcohol

The visualized muscle bulk is unremarkable.

Conclusion:
1. Degenerative radial tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Underlying severe degenerative changes of the lateral meniscus with apical fraying.
2. Oblique tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface.
3. Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No acute bony contusions.
4. Moderate femorotibial osteoarthritis with severe chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment as described in detail above.
5. Mild joint effusion with intra-articular bodies.

Bone marrow signal is normal. No acute fracture or bone bruise.

Moderate joint effusion. Lobulated ganglion cysts from the medial and lateral gastrocnemius tendon origins. Minimal Baker cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

Lateral meniscus: There is evidence of a small undersurface tear at the lateral meniscal body. Slight fraying of the inner margin along the posterior horn.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is moderate cartilage loss at the lateral patellar facet and lateral trochlea. Cartilage thinning/fissuring is present at the median ridge of the patella and at the central trochlea. Medial patellofemoral cartilage appears intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Slight lateral patellar subluxation. Patella alta. Findings suggest underlying patellar maltracking. The trochlear sulcus demonstrates normal depth. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:


1. Moderate patellofemoral chondrosis. Evidence of underlying patellar maltracking.

2. Evidence of a small tear of the lateral meniscus. Cartilage fissuring at the lateral tibial plateau.

3. Moderate joint effusion. Ganglion cysts arising from the medial and lateral gastrocnemius origins.

Hallazgos:
No hay alteración de señal difusa de la médula ósea.
Focos de edema óseo post contusionales en tercio medio de carga del cóndilo femoral lateral y
aspecto posterior del platillo tibial lateral.
Engrosamiento, alteración de señal y disrupción completa de las fibras del ligamento cruzado
anterior en tercio medio / distal. Se acompaña de traslación anterior de la tibia en
aproximadamente 13 mm.
Ligamentos cruzado posterior y colaterales continuos. Engrosamiento con leve alteración de señal
del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Menisco medial de morfología conservada con alteración de señal del cuerno posterior que no
cumple criterios de rotura. Destaca leve edema en la interfase meniscocapsular del cuerno
posterior del menisco medial.
Rotura longitudinal vertical en la periferia del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral en sitio inserción
del ligamento menisco femoral de Wrisberg.
Alteración de señal e irregularidad superficial del cartílago femorotibial, sin defectos condrales
profundos.
Cartílago rotuliano con alteración de señal e irregularidad superficial en faceta lateral y medial.
Úlcera condral de espesor subtotal con componente delaminativo, sin cambios óseos reactivos en
vertiente medial, región central y vertiente lateral de la tróclea, se extiende 13 mm medio lateral y
10 mm craneocaudal.
Perdida de tensión del tendón rotuliano.
Restantes tendones regionales de espesor y señal conservados.
Acentuado derrame articular. No se observa quiste de Baker.
Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo y de los planos intermusculares.

Rotura completa del LCA con contusiones óseas en cóndilo femoral lateral y platillo tibial lateral,
sugerentes de evento de inestabilidad reciente.
Esguince grado I del componente superficial del LCM.
Edema la interfase meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior del menisco medial, pudiera traducir
lesión a este nivel.
Rotura vertical periférica del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral en sitio de inserción del
ligamento menisco femoral posterior (de Wrisberg).
Condropatía femorotibial superficial. Condropatía rotuliana superficial. Defecto condral grado 2-3 que compromete vertiente medial, región central y vertiente lateral de la
tróclea.
Acentuado derrame articular.

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing and maceration of the body of medial meniscus with severe extrusion. Reactive marrow edema along the medial tibial plateau.
Medial compartment cartilage: Moderate cartilage loss throughout the medial compartment.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Inner margin blunting of the body of lateral meniscus.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Moderate cartilage loss with areas of full-thickness fissuring throughout the lateral compartment. No marrow edema,

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage loss throughout the lateral patellar median ridge and medial patella with subchondral cystic change. High-grade cartilage loss throughout the trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. There is marked MCL bursitis. 

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body with severe extrusion. 
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, severe in the patellofemoral compartment. If there is persistent pain, geniculate nerve ablation can be considered. 
3.	There is marked MCL bursitis. 
4.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis without tear.

Alignment is anatomic. Acute nondisplaced fracture of the posterior lateral tibial plateau with associated bone marrow edema. Edema extends to the tibial attachment of the posterior cruciate ligament. Small subchondral fracture at the periphery of the weightbearing surface of the lateral femoral condyle with bone marrow edema. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate hemarthrosis. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Mild edema along the myotendinous junction of the proximal popliteus muscle.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.

Aside from that described above, no acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Small amount of prepatellar subcutaneous edema.

IMPRESSION:
1. Acute nondisplaced fracture of the lateral tibial plateau.

4. Moderate hemarthrosis.

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness chondral fissuring at the lateral patellar facet and lateral trochlea with subchondral cystic change. Partial-thickness chondral fissuring spanning the trochlear notch.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Findings suggestive of lateral patellofemoral maltracking with high-grade patellofemoral compartment chondrosis, Hoffa's fat pad impingement, elevated TT-TG distance, and mild patellar tendinosis.

Collateral ligaments are intact.

No joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. Severe cartilage loss in the patella with 5 mm focus of bony edema at the lateral patellar apex. Moderate cartilage irregularity along the trochlea. Moderate cartilage thinning in the medial femoral condyle with no cartilage defects.

IMPRESSION:

No internal derangement.

Mild tendinosis of the proximal patellar tendon just inferior to the patella consistent with jumpers knee. No underlying patellar bony edema.

There is focal severe chondromalacia patella at the lateral patellar apex.

There is a moderate knee joint effusion with synovitis. There is no popliteal cysts.

Otherwise the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the pes anserine tendons, the semimembranosus, the popliteus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Moderate to severe degenerative changes most pronounced medially.

2. Diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration, extrusion and degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus. Intrasubstance degeneration of the lateral meniscus without tear.

3. Intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the ACL without ligament injury.

4. Knee joint effusion with synovitis without popliteal cyst.

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Mild reactive subchondral bone marrow edema at the weightbearing aspect of the medial compartment near the medial joint line. Medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartment marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Moderate Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a meniscal flap at the posterior horn. Displacement of a meniscal flap into the tibiomeniscal recess. Severe meniscal body extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade articular cartilage loss of the weightbearing aspect of the joint with confluent areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity and diffuse low grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with areas of high-grade fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Confluent full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the patella with subchondral signal changes. Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss of the trochlea with regions of full-thickness loss.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No lateral patellar tilt. Mild lateral patellar translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Severe patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment osteoarthritis. Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a small meniscal flap at the posterior horn-root junction. Severe meniscal extrusion.
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion. Moderate leaking Baker's cyst.

Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Suspect remote pivot shift injury with:
1. Complete tear of the midsubstance of the anterior cruciate ligament.

3. Low grade 2 sprain of the proximal medial collateral ligament

Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle with areas of full-thickness fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity at the patella and trochlea with large confluent regions of full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial patellar facet and full-thickness fissuring throughout the trochlea.

Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

There is horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus surfacing inferiorly. There is a small meniscal flap in the medial tibial gutter with reactive subjacent tibial bone marrow edema. A second meniscal flap is seen in the posterior intercondylar notch adjacent to the posterior root measuring 1.2 cm. The medial meniscus is mildly extruded. There are adjacent small Parameniscal cysts posteriorly.
There is complete tear of the medial collateral ligament, involving both the deep and superficial components at the femoral attachment with mild retraction. The femoral attachment of the medial patellofemoral ligament is also likely injured with adjacent edema.
There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
No meniscal tear is identified.
Lateral collateral ligament complex is intact.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
The posterior cruciate ligament demonstrates irregularity and increased signal intensity likely representing high-grade tear. There a few residual fibers, but this could be functionally complete tear. There is edematous changes around the meniscofemoral ligament likely representing sprain.
Anterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
There is small bony fragments at the medial attachment of patellar ligament with minimal to mild bone marrow changes likely representing remote Osgood-Schlatter.
There is diffuse mild to moderate cartilage thinning with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the trochlea.

Bones:
There is associated bone marrow edema involving the medial femoral epicondyle, with possible mild impaction within the posterior aspect. Bone marrow changes within the medial aspect of the fibula likely associated with degenerative changes.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

1.Horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with associated parameniscal cyst and two meniscal flap, as detailed above.
2.Complete tear of the medial collateral ligament involving both the deep and superficial components.

MRI of Left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, AX T2W FS


> Mild thickening of quadriceps tendon with increased signal intensity on F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
> Linear and blurring hyperintensity in the posterior horn of medial meniscus with articular surface disruption, in favor of longitudinal tear(srs 3001 img4-5)
> Mild increased intensity in the lateral meniscus, in favor intrasubstance degeneration
>The contour of ACL is not all in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, R/O mucoid degenration and partial tear
> There was no abnormal intensity in the PCL
> Wearing articular cartilage of knee joint with large spur formation and tiny subchondral cysts, more severe at medial compartment, reflecting osteoarthritis. 
> Focal increased intensity in the patellar cartilage with fissure and tiny subchondral cyst, more prominent at medial side, in favor of grade 4 chondral injury.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Subcutaneous infiltration with heterogenous enhancement noted in the prepatellar to infrapatellar region, edematous change 
> A small lobulated cystic lesion in popliteal fossa with a small recess of the knee joint capsule lies medially between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of small Baker's cyst.

Impression:
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee.
2. Synovitis of left knee joint with grade 4 chondromalacia.
3. R/O mucoid degenration and partial tear of AXL. 
4. Subcutanoeus infilammation over prepatellar to infrapatellar region.
5. Degeneration and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe longitudinal tear.
6. R/O synovial cyst or paramenical cyst in anterior intercondylar region of left knee.
7. Mild Anserine bursitis.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and lab data.

> MRI of knee was performed in sagittal, axial and coronal sections.
> Spin echo sequence were used.

> Comminuted fracture of right lateral tibial condyle with depressed, involving articular surface and tibial intercondylar eminence and in favor of avulsion fracture of ACL.
> The contour of ACL is not all in a straight line with increase signal intensity inside, R/O grade 2 injury.
> The contour of PCL is intact but increase signal intensity inside, R/O grade 1 injury.
> The contour of medial and lateral patellar retinaculum are not intact with increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 2 injury.
> The contour of MCL and LCL is intact with mild increase infiltration surrounding it, in favor of grade 1 sprain.
> Subcutaneous soft tissue swelling around knee joint, major at lateral side, r/o contusion injury.
> Presence of fluid-fluid level in the knee joint is noted, in favor of hemoarthrosis.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Significant bone marrow edema at patella, proximal tibia, and distal femur, major at lateral tibial condyle, r/o bone contusion.
> Increased infiltration over vastus lateralis, biceps femoris, muscles of anterior and lateral compartment of proximal leg, r/o muscle strain/edema.
> No evidence of tear in medial meniscus in this study.
    Suspicious of meniscocapsular separation of anterior lateral meniscus with increased signal intensity at meniscal meniscal root, R/O tear.
> increased signal intensity of the femoral original site of lateral collateral ligament, R/O grade 2-3 injury
> Mild degeneration of knee joint with spur formation

Impression:
1. Right tibial plateau fracture (Schatzker type II), and bone contusion at patella, proximal tibia, and distal femur.
2. R/O tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
3. In favor of grade 2 injury of ACL, and R/O grade 1 injury of PCL.
4. R/O grade 2-3 injury of lateral collateral ligament
5. Hemoarthrosis with synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis.
6. Subcutaneous contusion injury around knee joint, major at lateral side.
7. R/O muscle strain/edema at vastus lateralis, biceps femoris, and muscles of anterior and lateral compartment of proximal leg.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management.

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Ultrasound raise the possibility of meniscal tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The medial meniscus shows an inferiorly surfacing oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with tiny adjacent meniscal cysts. There is slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The posterior root and anterior horn are intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

No patellofemoral subluxation. The patellar retinacula are intact. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the patellofemoral compartment. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis. There is mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis with slight thinning of articular cartilage along the central weightbearing aspect of the condyle.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Inferiorly suspected complete tear of the junction of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with tiny adjacent parameniscal cyst and slight peripheral medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Subtle tricompartment chondrosis suggesting evolving mild osteoarthritis of the left knee.

There is edema and soft tissue stranding in the popliteal fossa

Bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus associated with moderate articular chondrosis to the articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle. Associated meniscal/parameniscal cyst arising at the posterior root of medial meniscus.

МР находка: МР данни за латерална луксация на пателата. Пателарният хрущял е лизиран почти изцяло, както и хрущяла по сътветстващата ставна повърхност на латералния февморален кондил. Стеснено е ретропателарното ставно пространство. Изобразуяват се малки субхондрални кисти и оток на костиня мозък в пателата и латералния феморален къндил, под увредения хрущял. Този лигамент е с изтънен напечник и повишен сигнален интензитет. Вижда се мекотъканен оток около пателата. Наличие на ставен излив. Vidi se multifragmentarna intraartikularna fraktura lateralnog platoa tibije koja se koso širi u područje interkondilarnih eminencija s  dislokacijom koštanih ulomka uz okolni koštani edem. Nepravilne zone koštanog edema u području lateralnog kondila tibije femura te manji areali koštanog edema medijalnog kondila tibije i oba kondila femura. 
Fraktura proksimalnog dijela fibule ispod glavice, bez pomaka uz okolni koštani edem. 
Subhondralno u lateralnom kondilu femura polumjesčasta T1 i PDFS hipointezivna zona LL promjera 9 mm, AP promjera 15 mm, uz okolni edem i blagi konveksitet kortikalisa - moguća osteohondralna lezija IIa. 
Opsežan edem mekih tkiva koljena.
Veća količina izljeva suprapatelarno te manja količina u medijalnom i lateralnom recesusu, intraartikularno te uz hvatište patelarnog ligamenta za tibiju. 
Prednji križni ligament promjenjenog intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta uz avulziju tibijalnog hvatišta.
Stražnji križni ligament urednog signala te se prati u kontinuitetu.
Prednji korijen lateralnog meniska povišenog intenziteta signala u smislu distenzije s parcijalnom rupturom dok je sam lateralni mensik bez znakova rupture. Ruptura posteroinferiornih vlakana popliteomeniscealnih fascikula.
Medijalni menisk bez znakova degeneracije ili rupture.
Parcijalna ruptura distalnog dijela medijalnog kolateralnog ligamenta.
Parcijalna ruptura lateralnog kolateralnog ligamenta neposredno pred hvatište za lateralni epikondil femura.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

4. Grade 1 injury of ACL
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

МР находка: МР данни за частична руптура на предна кръстна връзка. Лезията е в областта на горната една втора на връзката, където тя е с повишен напречник и повишен сигнален интензитет- находката е съответстваща на дезорганизирани съединително тъканни влакна, оток и хематом. Задната кръстна връзка е интактна. Вижда се малък отграничен костномозъчен едем в медиалното тибиално плато разположено отзад. Нормално изобразяване на латерален менискус. МР данни за малка лезия в заден рог на медиален мениск- 2а grade. Наличие на малка течна, вероятно хеморагична колекция около m.semimembranosus dex. Не се визуализира промяна в тялото на мускула или в неговото сухожилие. Изобразява се малък ставен излив. Ставният хрущял е със запазена дебелена, без промени в структурата. Нормално изобразяване на пателата, хрущяла на пателата и ретинакулуми. Колатерални лигаменти– б.о. Заключение: МР данни за частична руптура на предна кръстна връзка. Вътреставен излив. Лезия IIа grade на заден рог на медиален мениск. 

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

МР находка: Няма данни за ставен излив. Костите, формиращи дясната колянна става, са с нормална форма и сигнален интензитет. Ставният хрущял на фемура, тибията, и пателата е съхранен. Предната и задната кръстна връзка са със запазена цялост.  МР данни за лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус – 2а grade. Предният рог медиалния менискус е интактен. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Нормално изобразяване на латералния и медиалния колатерален лигамент. Патела, ретинакулуми – нормално изобразяване. Лигамент на пателата и сухожилие на мускулус квадрицепс феморис - нормално изобразяване. Меки тъкани и поплитеална ямка – б.о. Заключение: МР данни за лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус – 2а степен.

-SG PD FatSat, Locator, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, Sag T2W STIR, AX T2W STIR

> Wearing of articular cartilage and subchondral bone marrow edema and tiny subchondral cyst of right knee, more prominent at medial femoral conylde and tibial plateau; spur formation also noted.. 
> Some circumscribed abnormal bone marrow signal foci in right distal femur with hypointensity lines, major at epimetaphysis, R/O bone infarcts.
> Varocise veins, more prominent at lateral side.

1. C/W osteoarthritis of right knee joint, more severe at medial compartment.
2. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus and R/O tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
3. R/O grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL, PCL and MCL.
4. Synovitis of right knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
5. Baker's cyst.
6. R/O small bone infarcts of right dital femur.
7. Varicose veins.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Echogenic mass seen laterally in the right knee on ultrasound. Suggest for MRI evaluation.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
No prior imaging available for evaluation.

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No definite meniscal tear, no evidence of para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intrasubstance degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is slightly laterally subluxed. Lateral trochlear inclination angle is borderline, measuring approximately 11 degrees. TT TG distance is not increased. Insall Salvati ratio is 1.4, which is also within normal range. Thickening of the lateral retinaculum may be due to prior subluxation. Increased fat attenuation is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.

Fluid

Small joint effusion is seen. No loose body. Small Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss most observable at the lateral patella facet and apex associated subchondral chondral edema. Chondral irregularity at the trochlea is also seen associated with subchondral cysts.


Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Increasing fat signal is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.
Otherwise no focal soft tissue mass detected at the knee.

Severe chondral loss at the patellofemoral compartment particularly involving the lateral patella facet and apex associated with marked subchondral edema and subchondral cysts at both the femoral trochlea and patella. Patella is slightly laterally subluxed with borderline lateral trochlear inclination angle but normal Insall Salvati ratio and TT TG distance.

Артикулиращият ставен хрущял на фемура и тибията е със запазена дебелина и конгурентност по цялото си протежение. Патела - б.о. Хрущял на пателата – вижда се калък дефект с кос ход, както при начална хондромалация срединно в хрущяла на пателата. Ретинакулуми на пателата – със запазена цялост. В задният рог на медиалния менискус се вижда хиперинтензна линия с хоризонтален към кос ход, която не достига до артикулиращата ставна повърхност на тибията – скъсваане 2а стадий. Нормално изобразяване на предния рог на медиалния менискус и на латералния менискус. Нормално изобразяване на предната и задната кръстна връзка.

Il y a une petite déchirure oblique à la jonction de la corne postérieure et du corps du ménisque externe. Il n'y a pas de fragment méniscal déplacé.

Le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe est intact et sans déchirure. 

Il y a une atténuation modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémorotibial externe avec une fissure chondrale transfixiante au versant fémoral et des changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés.

Il y a un épaississement et un hypersignal plus marqué du ligament croisé antérieur à sa portion moyenne et proximale suggérant une entorse de grade intermédiaire/déchirure partielle. Il y a également une légère délamination/déchirure longitudinale interstitielle de bas grade des fibres moyennes et proximales du ligament croisé postérieur. Il n'y a pas d'évidence d’atteinte transfixiante des ligaments croisés.

L’alignement patellofémoral est préservé. Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts et sans déchirure. 

Conclusion :

Il y a une fracture trabéculaire sous-chondrale par impaction au versant postérieur du plateau tibial externe, sans dépression de la surface articulaire. Il y a un œdème osseux significatif associé tel que détaillé ci-haut. 

Il y a une entorse de grade 1 du ligament collatéral interne avec une petite contusion osseuse associée au condyle fémoral interne. 

Il y a une entorse de grade intermédiaire/déchirure partielle du ligament croisé antérieur. Il y a une délamination/déchirure longitudinale interstitielle de bas grade du ligament croisé postérieur. Il n'y a pas d’atteinte transfixiante des ligaments croisés. 

Il y a une petite déchirure oblique à la jonction de la corne postérieure et du corps du ménisque externe. Il n'y a pas de fragment méniscal déplacé. 

Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire. 

Il n'y a pas de fracture rotulienne.

Constatations : 

Il y a un épanchement articulaire modéré avec des signes de synovite.

Il n'y a pas de kyste poplité.

La rotule est positionnée un peu haute (rotule alta). De plus, il y a une légère bascule externe de la rotule, sans évidence par contre de subluxation.

Il y a une légère tendinopathie du tendon rotulien. Il n'y a pas de bursite, mais il y a un œdème antérieur au tendon rotulien qui descend jusqu’à la tubérosité tibiale. Le rétinaculum interne de la rotule est un peu irrégulier. La graisse de Hoffa est normale. Le gras suprarotulien est également normal.

Il y a une chondrose de grade 2 à 3 du cartilage fémororotulien. 

Il y a une déchirure ancienne du ménisque interne. Elle implique la racine de la corne postérieure qui démontre une augmentation du signal avec des signes de macération. Cela explique l’extrusion significative du corps du ménisque interne avec un œdème intrasubstance. Il y a une légère extrusion aussi de la corne antérieure de ce ménisque.

Le ménisque externe ne démontre pas d’anomalie significative.

Le ligament croisé antérieur ne démontre pas de déchirure. 

Le ligament croisé postérieur est normal.

Le complexe ligamentaire externe ne démontre pas d’anomalie significative.

Le ligament collatéral interne est bombé vu l’extrusion du ménisque interne. Il est un peu épaissi aussi à sa partie supérieure témoignant d’une ancienne entorse. Il n'y a pas de déchirure.

Il y a de l’œdème de la moelle osseuse au coin du plateau tibial interne en relation avec cette déchirure du ménisque interne. Il y a également une chondrose de grade 2 à 3 du compartiment tibiofémoral interne avec un pincement articulaire.

Le reste de l’examen est sans particularité. 

Conclusion :

L’anomalie principale est cette déchirure ancienne du ménisque interne. Vu que la racine de la corne postérieure est déchirée, il y a une extrusion complète du corps et une légère extrusion de la corne antérieure. Cela veut dire que le ménisque ne sert plus sa fonction. D’ailleurs, il y a un pincement articulaire du compartiment interne avec une chondrose de grade 2 à 3. Il y a aussi des changements de stress en périphérie du plateau tibial interne tels que décrits plus haut. Cela peut évidemment causer de la douleur à la marche et en position debout. Une corrélation clinique est recommandée. 

Ancienne entorse du ligament collatéral interne. 

Rotule un peu alta avec une légère tendinopathie du tendon rotulien.

Chondrose de grade 2 à 3 du cartilage fémororotulien.

Épanchement articulaire avec synovite.

Autres observations faites; voir rapport plus haut.

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated 
knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow

osseous lesions.

Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, partially 
ruptured Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Peripheral vertical tear of the posterior horn extending 
to the body.

Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Areas of full-thickness cartilage 
loss along the medial facet and median ridge as well as central trochlea 
with underlying subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete tear of the midportion of the 
ACL.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 2 sprain of the 
popliteofibular ligament. Periligamentous edema about the lateral 
collateral ligament with intact fibers.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. Ganglion cyst of the popliteus 
tendon sheath.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.

lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and 
trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) 
distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not 
previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. 
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Venous 
fluid-fluid level in the popliteal fossa.

to the body of the medial meniscus.

МР находка: МР данни за дегенеративна промяна и лезия на задния рог на медиалиня менискус. Задният рог на медиалния менискус е с повишен интензитет на сигнала, като сред него се изобразява хиперинтензна линия с радиерен ход, съответстваща на скъсване. Скъсването достига до края на менискуса и да хрущяла на тибията. Съвразана със задния рог на медиалния менискус се вижда голяма мултилокуларна киста. Кистата се проектира зад менискуса и от латералната и медиалната му страна. Латералният менискус е с нормална големина, форма и континуитет. Наличие на малък ставен излив. Костите, формиращи лявата колянна става, са с нормална форма. Изобразява се малка зона на костно-мозъчен едем в латералната интеркондиларн еминенция на тибията.  Ставният хрущял на фемура, тибията и пателата е интактен. Предната и задната кръстна връзка са със запазена цялост.  Нормално изобразяване на латералния и медиалния колатерален лигамент. Патела, ретинакулуми на пателата – нормално изобразяване. Лигамент на пателата и сухожилие на мускулус квадрицепс феморис - нормално изобразяване. Поплитеална ямка – б.о. Заключение:  
МР данни за дегенеративна промяна и скъсване на задния рог на медиалния менискус – grade 3. Киста на задния рог на медиалния менискус.

No significant knee effusion, there are no intra-articular bodies either.  
Multilocular cystic mass posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament, deep to the popliteal neurovascular bundle, in keeping with a ganglion cyst that is arising from the knee joint proper.
There is a complex, undisplaced tear through the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
There is associated high signal within the subchondral bone of the lateral aspect of the medial tibial plateau, potentially representative of a bone marrow contusion. 
Any history of direct trauma to account for such appearances?
The lateral meniscus is intact, as are the cruciate and collateral ligaments, distal iliotibial band, popliteus musculotendinous unit, extensor tendons in the remaining marrow signal throughout.
High-riding patella noted, together with pre femoral fat pad impingement - any history of anterior knee pain?
Solitary grade 3 cartilage fissure noted at the medial retropatellar facet.
Tricompartmental articular cartilage is otherwise well preserved.  
Anterior subcutaneous edema like signal change with no discrete bursal formation, kindly correlate clinically.
Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues. 

Impression:
Complex undisplaced medial meniscal tear.
Focal medial retropatellar cartilage damage.
Multifactorial low grade extensor mechanism pathology.
Suspected posteromedial proximal tibial bone marrow contusion.

Налице е и лезия с остеосклеротичен вал и нееднороден кистичен център. Находката е с размери 9/6.5мм, разположена в метаепифизарно в медиалния кондил на фемура. Останалите кости, формиращи дясната колянна става са с нормална форма и сигнална характеристика. Малък дефект в хрущяла на фемура. Дефектът е разположен срединно, ретропателарно, без данни за формиране на остеоходнрален фрагмент. Визуализира се хиперинтензна лезия в задния рог на медиалния менискус – grade IIb. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Кръстни връзки – със запазена цялост. Колатерални лигаменти – нормално изобразяване. Wiberg I патела. Insall-Salvati-0.8. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис и лигамент на пателата – б.о. Заключение: МР данни за остеохондром на фемура с описаната локализация. Il n’y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif au genou.

Il n’y a pas de kyste poplité. Minime liséré de liquide dans la bourse semi-membraneuse.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts. Il y a une structure ovoïde liquidienne de 0.6 x 0.4 x 0.3cm entre les ligaments croisés qui pourrait refléter une petite loculation du liquide intra-articulaire VS un petit kyste ganglionnaire (image 19, série 3).

Il y a des fissure de cartilage de grade modéré à haut à la facette médiale et à la crête médiane de la rotule. Il y a aussi des changements de signal au cartilage de la facette latérale de la rotule suggérant une chondropathie débutante. Il y a des fissure de grade modéré à l’aspect inférieur de la trochlée particulièrement à son aspect central et médial. Minime quantité de liquide dans la bourse infra-patellaire profonde.

Compartiment interne :

Léger amincissement de cartilage diffus. Le ménisque interne et le ligament collatéral interne sont sans particularité.

Compartiment externe :

Légère chondropathie. Il y a des changements de signal hyperintense T2 intrasubstance à la corne antérieure/racine antérieure du ménisque latéral suggérant des changements dégénératifs. Le complexe ligamentaire latéral est sans particularité.

Conclusion :

Chondropathie modérée au compartiment antérieur et légère au compartiment interne et externe.

Il n’y a pas de kyste poplité.

Il y a un probable kyste ganglionnaire de 6mm entre les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur.

Blagi hiperintenziteti stražnjih dijelova pri hvatištima patelarnog ligamenta - moguće uslijed

МР находка: Вижда се малка остеохондрална лезия на пателарната ставна повърхност на бедрената кост, по срединна линия. Под дефекта се изобразява ограничен костномозъчен едем. Не се виждат промени в ставния хрущял по медиалния и латералния кондил на фемура, както и на тибията. Патела, хрущял на пателата – б.о. Наличие на ставен излив. Вижда се мултилокуларна Бекерова киста стипична локализация между сухожилията на м. семимембранозус и м.семитендинозус. Кистата е с овална форма и размери 65/19 мм. Част от кистата е руптурирала, като течно съдържимо от нея е десцендирало и се намира около мускулните групи на м. гастрокнемиус. Вижда се малка мултилокуларна киста, разположена до ставната капсула и задната кръстна връзка. Кръстните връзки са интактни.
МР данни за частично, минимално скъсване на медиалния колатерален лигамент с давност. Латерален колатерален лигамент – б.о. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – б.о. МР данни за инсерционит на лигамента на пателата. Вижда се високосигнална зона на залавното място на лигамента към пателата. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. МР данни за дегенеративна промяна в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Задния рог на медиалния менискус е с висок интензитет на сигнала. Няма данни за фрагментиране на менискуса. Инсерционит на лигамента на пателата. Ставен излив. Бекерова киста, част от кистата е руптурирала. Частично, минимално скъсване с давност на медиалния колатерален лигамент.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Osteoarthritis.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Bone marrow edema at the medial tibial plateau, likely reactive. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion, incompletely imaged, with synovial proliferation. Trace leaking Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn, with dominant complete radial tear at the posterior horn-root junction. Moderate meniscal body extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity with areas of full-thickness fissuring at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Degeneration without discrete tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse low-grade cartilage loss at the patella with areas of full-thickness fissuring at the lateral and medial facets. Focal high-grade cartilage loss of the central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Mild mucoid degeneration.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Patellar enthesopathy. Mild patellar tendinosis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 10 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Fluid tracking into the popliteus tendon sheath.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant complete radial component at the posterior horn-root junction. Moderate meniscal body extrusion.
2.	Bone marrow edema at the medial tibial plateau, concerning for early subchondral insufficiency fracture.
3.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, overall mild to moderate. Moderate knee joint effusion. Trace leaking Baker's cyst.
4.	Mild distal quadriceps and patellar tendinosis.

In the medial compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is displaced meniscal fragment into the medial gutter. There is diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis (less than and more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along weightbaring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is subchondral edema. Few subchondral bone cysts (about intact2intact3 cm) are present. Osteophytes are present. 
  
 The lateral compartment, there is complex tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is diffuse low grade chondrosis along weightbaring, non weightbaring lateral femoral condyle. Diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis along lateral tibial plateau. There is subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present.  
  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial trochlea. There is no subchondral edema. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior cruciate ligament is intact. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no tibial translation. 
  
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Minimal amount of right knee effusion is present. There is a 2* intact5* 4.5 cm baker's cyst at the posteromedial aspect of the right knee. The surrounding musculature is normal.  Mild to moderate medial tibiofemoral compartmental osteoarthritis of the right knee by evidence of chondrosis, subchondral edema, cyst and osteophytes.

Na seriji MR presjeka lijevog koljena vidi se koštani edem medijalnog kondila femura i platoa
tibije uz potpuno reduciranu debljinu artikulacijske hrskavice medijalnog kondila femura i platoa
tibije te vidljivu manju zonu subhondralnog edema posteriornog dijela kondila femura
(hondromalacija IV. stupnja). Masivni osteofiti medijalnog kondila femura i platoa tibije. Uredna
je morfologija i intenziteti signala lateralnog kolateralnog kompleksa, stražnjeg križnog
ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarnog ligamenta i tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Blaža mukoidna degeneracija prednjeg križnog ligamenta uz vidljive sitne cistične degenerativne
promjene pri tibijalnom hvatištu.
Periligamentarni edem MCL u sklopu OA promjena.
Kompleksna ruptura stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska na degenerativnoj podlozi. Vidi se defekt
dijela tijela medijalnog meniska uz ekstruziju istog.
Kompleksna ruptura stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska (horizontalna i dominantno
longitudinalna).
Vide se fissure medijalne fasete patele koje zahvaćaju >50% površine (hondromalacija III.
stupnja).
Značajno je reducirana debljina artikulacijske hrskavice medijalne i lateralne trohleje femura.
Manja zona subhondralnog koštanog edema medijalne trohleje femura.
Hondromalacija II./III. stupnja lateralnog platoa tibije.
Opsežan izljev u koljenu, dominantno u suprapatelarnom recessusu. Ne nalazi se poplitealne
(Bakerove) ciste.
Edem Hoffine masti - ddg. impigement.
Unutar masnog tkiva, s dorzalne strane distalne dijametafize femura vidi se cistična lezija
promjera 21 mm.
Manja količina lokulirane tekućine unutar lateraelnog dijela m. popliteusa prema
mišićno-tetivnom prijelazu te između m. popliteusa i lateralna glave m. gastrocnemiusa.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild diffuse cartilage thinning with small foci of full-thickness fissuring along the weightbearing medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild heterogeneity and low-grade fissuring along the posterior weightbearing lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the lateral facet with chondral fissuring along at the junction of the medial facet/median ridge.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Mild patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, most significant in the patellofemoral compartment.
2.	Small joint effusion.
