Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Three-week history of left knee pain after slipping on a wet floor and slamming knee into wall.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Osseous contusion involving the anterior peripheral aspect of the medial femoral condyle. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal spurring, most notably along the medial tibiofemoral compartment.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate complex multilobulated Baker's cyst with calcified bodies and synovial proliferation.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex degenerative tearing involving the anterior horn, body and posterior horn medial meniscus with severe meniscal extrusion of the body and displaced fragment within the meniscotibial recess. Superimposed reactive marrow edema at the medial tibial margin.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse full-thickness cartilage loss about the weightbearing medial femoral condyle with scattered areas of subchondral marrow edema and cystic change. Additional diffuse cartilage loss along the anterior and central medial tibial plateau with scattered subchondral marrow edema.


LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Degenerative signal posterior horn and posterior root with suspected degenerative tearing at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. No meniscal extrusion or displaced fragment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss/fraying about the central weightbearing lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal partial thickness chondrosis central femoral trochlea. Patellar cartilage is intact. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Bowing of the medial meniscus secondary to adjacent medial meniscal pathology. Otherwise intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 1 sprain characterized by periligamentous edema.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific subcutaneous soft tissue edema about the anterior knee. Mild deep infrapatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Osseous contusion involving the anterior peripheral medial femoral condyle.
2.	Complex tearing of the anterior horn to posterior horn medial meniscus with severe meniscal extrusion of the body and displaced fragment within the meniscotibial recess.
3.	Tricompartmental chondrosis and osteoarthritis, severe involving the medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4.	Grade 1 sprain LCL.
5.	Moderate complex Baker's cyst containing multiple calcified bodies.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Multifocal areas of subchondral edema along the lateral tibial plateau and femoral condyles. Fabella with edema. 

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small , partially ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Imaging of the ACL without tear..
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Periligamentous edema about the biceps femoris and lateral collateral ligament with intact fibers.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Small joint effusion with synovitis as well as subchondral marrow edema along both tibial plateau and femoral condyles and edema of the posterolateral corner. Findings are concerning for early inflammatory arthritis, for which aspiration should be considered.

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

1.	Subcutaneous soft tissue hematoma along the anterosuperomedial aspect of the knee measuring approximately 3.4 x 0.7 x 4.8 cm, interposed between subcutaneous soft tissue and the deep fascial layer (Morel-Lavallee lesion).

-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Ax T2 FS, Cor T2 FS, Sag T1, Screen Save, Sag T2 FS

* Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.

* Flattening of ACL slope and increased singal intensity, C/W ACL tear.
> The contour of PCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Hyperintensity foci of tibial intercondylar eminence on F/S T2WI, in favor of bone contusion.
> Lateral tilting of patella. Mild fraying surface of articular cartilage of patella.
> Increased fat stranding of infrapatellar fat pad.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of medial femoral condyle and medial and lateral tibial plateau, in favor of chondromalacia.
> Mild joint effusion and medial patellar plicae. 
Impression:
1. C/W ACL tear.
2. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. In favor of degeneration of tibial intercondylar eminence with bone marrow edema.
4. Mild osteoarthritis of left knee and grade 2 chondromalacia of left knee, major at medial compartment.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

Na seriji učinjenih MR presjeka kroz desno koljeno prikaže se kompletna radijalna ruptura
stražnjeg korijena medijalnog meniska s prema van zglobnog prostora ekstrudiranim preostalim
dijelom meniska i posljedično napetim prikazom medijalnog kolateralnog ligamenta.
Prisutne su osteoartrotske promjene femorotibijalno, izraženije medijalno s hondromalacijskim
lezijama 3.-4. stupnja oba femoralna kondila i platoa tibije.
Edem medijalnog femoralnog kondila i nešto manje medijalnog tibijalnog s aplaniranom nosivom
plohom medijalnog kondila femura i suphondralnom frakturom na arealu oko 8 mm (SIF).
Vidljivo je više slobodnih zglobnih tijela femorotibijalno, pojedini intenziteta kosti, a pojedini
hrskavice, a opisane su promjene u sklopu sekundarne sinovijalne osteohondromatoze.
Lateralni je menisk je bez znakova rupture.
Prednji i stražnji križni lateralni kolateralni ligament su održanog kontinuiteta, uredne debljine i
intenziteta signala, bez znakova lezije.
Mali intraartikularni izljev.
Izljev u bursi pes anserinusa aksijalnog promjera 3 cm, bez izljeva u Bakerovoj burzi.
Patela je asimetrična (Wiberg tip 3), a femoropatelarni zglob kongruentan s hondromalacijskim
lezijama 4. stupnja medijalne fasete i 2. stupnja grebena patele i femoralne trohlee.
Hipertrofična je medijalna patelarna plica, doseže zglobnu plohu medijalne fasete.
uredne debljine i intenziteta signala hrskavičnog pokrova patele i trohlee femura.
Uredan je prikaz tetive kvadricepsa, patelarnih retinakula i patelarne tetive, a TT-TG distanca
je u fiziološkim granicama.
Blagi edem mekog tkiva prepatelarno i medijalnog dijela supkutane masti koljena.
Na ostalim prikazanim koštanim, mekotkivnim i neurovaskularnim strukturama ne nalazim MR
znakova patomorfoloških promjena.

Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Derangement of anterior horn of medial meniscus of right knee due to old injury

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate suprapatellar joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is mild ill-defined increased signal intensity within the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus consistent with grade 2 degeneration. There is slight blunting at the root of the posterior horn which may represent a tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is mild chondromalacia.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is severe thinning of the patellar cartilage. There is mild thinning of the cartilage in the femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.


IMPRESSION:
1. Grade 2 degeneration of the medial meniscus with possible tear at the root.
2. Severe chondromalacia patella. Mild chondromalacia in the lateral joint compartment.
3. Moderate suprapatellar joint effusion.

MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Right knee instability. Anterior drawer test positive? Anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Mild hyperintensity is seen at the posterior horn suggestive of intrasubstance degeneration. No definite tear. No parameniscal cyst. 

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: Intact fibers are present however caliber of these fibers is somewhat attenuated compatible with a remote low-grade partial thickness injury. No significant tibial translation.

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Marked patella chondral hypertrophy is seen measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. It appears heterogeneously hyperintense with regions of hypointensity, possibly due to mineralization. No evidence of invasion into the patella bone. It is closely abutting a medial plica. A possible loose body is also seen. Suspicious fissure also observed at the apex. Findings non specific in nature but favours to represent severe chondromalacia. Differential diagnoses such as focal synovitis and PVNS are less probable. 

Medial compartment: Mild chondrosis of the medial femoral condyle.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondrosis of the lateral femoral condyle.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Low grade, remote, partial thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No tibial translation.

Marked heterogeneous hypertrophy of the articular cartilage of the patella measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. Signal in this irregular thickened cartilage is heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted imaging and shows focal regions of hypointensity which may represent mineralization. Findings are favored to represent severe chondropathic change involving the articular cartilage of the patella.

Das laterale Retinaculum nicht durchgehend abgrenzbar bei V. a. mit entsprechendem Tonusverlust und elongiert gewähltem Verlauf. Insall-Salvati Index von 1,1 somit kein, Patellahochstand. Kleine subkortikale Zyste an der lateralen Patellafacette (9/10). Moderate Chondropathie der Trochlea (z. B. 9/20). Zarte osteophytäre Anbauten lateralseitig (9/17).

Femorotibial lateralseitig am Tibiaplateau (6/27) sowie an der Femurkondyle (5/25) teilweise vollschichtige Chondropathie. Der Außenmeniskus im Vorderhorn und Pars intermedia deutlich substanzgemindert, im Hinterhorn aufgetrieben und massiv signalalteriert (6/25) mit Signalanhebungen bis in die hintere Wurzel. Deutliche osteophytäre Randanbauten.

Ruptur bei auf dem gastrocnemicus auslaufender Flüssigkeit. Ansonsten unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Weichteile.

Deutliche Ausdünnung des Knorpels femorotibial teils mit vollschichtig ausgedünntem Knorpelbesatz  (Serie 5/ Image 24) und fokalem subchondralem Knochenödem (Serie 5/ Image 20). Innenmeniskusextrusion in der Pars intermedia.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Geringe oberflächliche Irregularitäten des Knorpel femorotibial. Verdacht auf radiären Riss in der Pars intermedia des Außenmeniskus. Partialläsion des MCL bei angrenzend Flüssigkeit und geringen hyperintensen Signalalterationen.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Trochlea:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Fokaler tiefgreifender Defekt am inferioren Patellafirst (Serie 4/ Image 14). Kein subchondrales Knochenödem. Ansonsten intakter Knorpel. Regelrechte Darstellung der Patella- und Quadrizepssehne. Regelrechter Hoffa`scher Fettkörper.

Kreuzbänder:
Intakte Kreuzbänder.

Muskulatur und übrige Weichteile:
Mäßiger Gelenkerguss  mit verdickter Synovia. Regelrechtes flow-void in den erfassten Gefäßen.

Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 5 years of anterior knee pain
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Partial-thickness chondral fissuring in the posterior nonweightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness fissuring in the and medial patellar facet with subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Mild increased signal proximally which may represent early degenerative change versus chronic resolving low-grade injury. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear. Edema and thickening of the quadriceps fat pad which may be secondary to impingement.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Mild prepatellar edema.

IMPRESSION:
Possible quadriceps tendon impingement with subsequent full-thickness chondral fissuring of the medial patellar facet with subchondral edema.

Manja količina izljeva suprapatelarno.

intenziteta signala.

COMPARISON:Prior MRI scans from [Date] and [Date]. Plain films [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right knee pain, suspected meniscal pathology.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body without evidence of discrete medial meniscal tear.

The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the patellofemoral compartment. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Small knee joint effusion. Of note, there is an ovoid intramuscular lesion of low proton density/low T2 signal within the substance of the proximal fibers of the extensor digitorum muscle, measuring 33 mm craniocaudal, 15 mm anterior to posterior, 18 mm medial to lateral. The lesion shows a thin T2 hyperintense rim. This was not present on the recent prior MRI. The correlative plain films from [Date] show no evidence of focal mineralization in the region of the lesion.

Subcutaneous edema along the anterolateral aspect of the knee and proximal calf. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Interval development of a 33 x 15 x 18 mm intramuscular lesion within the proximal musculature of the anterior compartment of the right calf. Correlation with gadolinium-enhanced MRI recommended for complete assessment.
2. Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис и лигамент на пателата – б.о. Interprétation: 

Dans l’intervalle, il y a eu progression d’un épanchement intra-articulaire d’allure modérée à large avec signes de synovite chronique. Il y a également augmentation en taille d’un kyste de Baker multi-lobulé, non-compliqué s’étendant sur 4.4cm de diamètre CC. 

Il y a une déchirure légèrement complexe du ménisque interne dans l’intervalle avec une composante probablement longitudinale oblique à la jonction de la corne postérieure et du corps méniscal avec flap méniscal déplacé au sein de la gouttière antérosupérieure à l’interligne articulaire fémoro-tibial interne. Il y a extrusion modérée du ménisque résiduel. 

Il y a progression d’une chondropathie maintenant sévère (grade 4) au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne avec dénudation transfixiante des surfaces cartilagineuses et changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ostéophytes marginaux modérés. 

Le ligament collatéral interne est intact sans déchirure. 

Léger émoussement du rebord libre de la corne postérieur du ménisque externe sans déchirure méniscale significative. Atténuation chondrale légère à modérée au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe avec fissures chondrales partielles en lien avec une chondropathie de grade 2. Il n’y a pas d’évidence d’atteinte transfixiante ou changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ostéophytose modérée. Le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe est intact sans déchirure. Il y a multiples kystes ganglionnaires en lien avec la jonction myotendineuse et le récessus poplité au versant postéro-externe du genou. 

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. 

L’alignement fémoro-patellaire demeure dans les limites normales. Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts sans déchirure. Il y a une atténuation diffuse modérée des surfaces chondrales, avec foyer de chondropathie de grade 4 similaire le long de la facette patellaire interne avec fissure transfixiante et début de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés et de grade 3 au niveau de l’échancrure inter-condylienne avec fissure chondrale transfixiante. Petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Œdème sous-cutané pré-patellaire et infra-patellaire, non-spécifique. 

Conclusion: 

Il y a une nouvelle déchirure légèrement complexe dans l’intervalle impliquant le ménisque interne avec composante longitudinale oblique à la jonction de la corne postérieure et du corps méniscal et flap méniscal déplacé au sein de la gouttière antéro-supérieure à l’interligne articulaire fémoro-tibial interne tel que décrit ci-haut. 

Il y a progression d’une chondropathie fémoro-tibiale principalement interne, avec atteinte de grade 4. 

Progression d’un épanchement intra-articulaire maintenant modéré à large et d’un kyste de Baker non-compliqué avec signes de synovite associés. 

Il n’y a pas d’autre changement significatif dans l’intervalle incluant une chondropathie de grade 4 le long de la facette patellaire interne.

original_report: МР находка: МР данни за медиална гонартроза. Ставният хрущял на фемура и тибията от медиалната страна е изтънен. Наличие на ставна течност на мястото на лизирания хрущял. Дефекти в хрущяла на тибията се виждат и от латералната страна. Вижда се малка зона на субхондрален костно-мозъчен едем в медиалния кондил на фемура. Наличие на остеофитни наслоявания по кондилите на фемура и в по-лека степен на тибията. Остеофити се изобразяват и по интеркондиларните еминенции. Виждат се субхондрални кисти срединно в тибията. Наличие на малък ставен излив. Визуализира се голяма Бекерова киста с размер 74/24 мм. МР данни за изразени дегенеративни промени и руптура на медиалния менискус. Менискусът е увреден и се представя с повишен интензитет на сигнала и уголемен напречник, като същият е експулсиран встрани. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост. Малки остеофити се виждат и по краищата на пателата. Хрущяла на пателата е лекостепенно изтънен, без видими дефекти и без костномозъчен едем в нея. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Сухожилие на м.квадрицепс феморис, лигамент на пателата -нормално изобразяване. Колатерални лигаменти – б.о. Заключение: МР данни за медиална гонартроза. Увреден, експулсиран встрани медиален менискус.

Trouvailles :

Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire sans kyste poplité.

Il y a légers à modérés changements dégénératifs plus proéminent au niveau du compartiment interne. Plus précisément, il y a amincissement modéré du cartilage impliquant la partie centrale du condyle fémoral interne et du plafond tibial avec léger changement réactif sous-chondral. Il y a un amincissement modéré du cartilage à la facette médiale de la rotule et à la partie médiale et centrale de la trochlée du fémur. Il y a léger amincissement et fibrillation superficielle du compartiment externe.

Il y a changements dégénératifs intra-substance impliquant le corps et la corne postérieure du ménisque interne. Il y a une déchirure radiale complète de la jonction du corps et de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne avec extrusion du ménisque. Le ménisque externe démontre changements dégénératifs intra-substance sans déchirure linéaire bien définie.

Autrement le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et tendon du poplité, le biceps fémoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité.

Conclusion :

1. Changements dégénératifs légers à modérés plus proéminent au niveau du compartiment interne tel que détaillé ci-haut.

2. Changements dégénératifs intra-substance du ménisque interne avec déchirure radiale complète et extrusion du ménisque tel que détaillé ci-haut. Aucune déchirure linéaire du ménisque externe.

3. Épanchement intra-articulaire sans kyste poplité.

МР данни за дегенеративна промяна и лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус. Задният рог на медиалния менискус е с висок интензитет на сигнала. В него се вижда хиперинтензна линия с кос ход, съответстваща на скъсване. Скъсването достига до края на менискуса. МР данни за тендинит и частични скъсвания на лигамента на пателата и сухожилието на м. квадрицепс феморис.  По отношение на напречника на споменатите сухожилие и лигамент, увредата е около 50% и се намира на залавните им към пателата места. Латерален менискус – без особености. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост и сигнална характеристика. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Едем на меките тъкани около коляното. Clinical information: 7 days post soccer injury with valgus shift. Medial collateral ligament testing positive. Medial collateral ligament tear? Partial posterior cruciate ligament tear?

Technique: Unenhanced point tender multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
The medial and lateral meniscus are intact.

There is a slightly increased T2 signal within the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. The anterior cruciate ligament as a construct is intact. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. The collateral ligaments are intact.

The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a focal avulsed, unhealed bone fragment at the inferior patellar pole. There is no focal bone marrow edema.

There is a focal area of extensive subchondral bone marrow edema in the weightbearing portion of the lateral tibial plateau with associated, nondisplaced subchondral fracture (17-9). There is a focal area of subcortical bone marrow edema at the anterolateral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and at the anteromedial aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

There is a minimal superficial chondrosis in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with focal superficial cartilage delamination at the medial patellar facet measuring 0.4 cm from medial to lateral.

There is mild joint effusion. There is a low volume Baker's cyst. The Infrapatellar fat pad is intact.

Conclusion:
1. Nondisplaced, subchondral fracture of the lateral tibial plateau with associated bone marrow edema. Posttraumatic contusions at the anterior aspect of the medial and lateral femoral condyles.
2. Low-grade partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No acute injury of the medial collateral ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.
3. Previous unhealed avulsion fracture at the inferior patellar pole.
4. Moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with a focal area of cartilage delamination at the medial patellar facet.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Clicking, locking, exclude meniscal tear..

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination. The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta. The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.6.
The finding is associated with advanced patellofemoral joint osteoarthritic change with extensive denuding of the articular cartilage and with extensive subcortical cyst formation particularly seen along the apex and lateral facet of patella. Prominent trochlear and patellar osteophytes are demonstrated.

The medial patellar retinaculum is attenuated likely related to previous lateral dislocation and partial disruption. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

There is a degenerative medial meniscal tear. There is maceration and linear signal seen in the posterior horn extending into the body. An oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the body and posterior horn is a demonstrated. The finding is associated with severe chondral denuding and exuberant marginal osteophyte formation seen to the medial joint compartment. There is also subcortical edema seen to the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

The lateral meniscus is macerated and not identified at the body and posterior horn. Findings are in keeping with extensive maceration and degenerative tearing of the body and the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. The finding is associated with denuding of the entire articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment associated with prominent lateral joint compartment osteophyte formation. There is also subcortical sclerosis and mild edema seen within the lateral joint compartment. An intraosseous cyst is seen to the lateral femoral condyle with 3 cm in keeping with subcortical tear.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligament are intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is a large knee effusion with reactive synovitis. There is no significant Baker's cyst. In the lateral popliteal fossa there is a large intraosseous loose body projecting anterior to the proximal fibers of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius measuring about 2.4 cm in maximum dimension. Smaller loose bodies are likely present in this region.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritic change most severely affecting patellofemoral and lateral compartments. Degenerative meniscal tears laterally and medially with cartilaginous denuding to the lateral medial and patellofemoral compartments.

Loose bodies.

Patella alta with attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum likely related to prior transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

There is a large knee joint effusion with synovitis. There is no popliteal cysts.

There is diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration, extrusion and degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus demonstrates intrasubstance degeneration without a well-defined linear tear.

There is intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Otherwise the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the pes anserine tendons, the semimembranosus, the popliteus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Moderate to severe degenerative changes most pronounced in the lateral compartment with areas of full-thickness cartilage loss as detailed above.

2. Diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration and degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus with intrasubstance degeneration of the medial meniscus. There is no well-defined linear tear.

3. Intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the ACL without ligament injury.

4. Knee joint effusion with synovitis without popliteal cyst.

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of mid fibers of anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are demonstrated. Along the course of the anterior cruciate ligament there is amorphous increased T2 signal with fiber caliber expansion. The finding is associated with an anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 9 mm. There is associated buckling of the posterior cruciate ligament.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact and unremarkable otherwise.

The medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is no significant Baker's cyst.

There is mild prepatellar edema and edema overlying the lateral aspect of the knee.

There is a small knee effusion.

Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with anterior tibial drawer.

No significant meniscal tears.

Na učinjenim u sekvencama vidljiva je rekonverzija koštane srži u distalnoj dijametafizi femura.
Vidljive su manje zone koštanog edema oba kondila femura ispod hvatišta kolateralnih ligamenata. 
Manja zona edema u području interkondilarne eminencije tibije uz hvatište prednjeg križnog ligamenta i prednjeg korijena lateralnog meniska.
Vidljiva je hondromalacija IV. stupnja patelarne hrskavica uz zone erozije hrskavice u centralnom dijelu i prema lateralnoj faseti.
U lateralnom dijelu trohleje femura nalazi se zona denudacije zglobne hrskavice uz subhondralni edem - također hondromalacija IV.stupnja. Rubna osteofitoza zglobnih tijela u sklopu osteoartritičkih promjena.
Vidljive su i erozije zglobnih hrskavica femorotibijalnog zgloba, izraženije u medijalnom kompartmentu. Opisano odgovara hondromalaciji III. stupnja.
Prednji i stražnji križni ligament su održanog kontinuiteta, primjerenih intenziteta signala.
Degenerativno promijenjen lateralni menisk, moguća manja kosa ruptura stražnjeg roga meniska.
Degenerativno promijenjen medijalni menisk, bez evidentne rupture.
Ruptura anterolateralnog ligamenta koljena.
Medijalni kolateralni lateralni kolateralni ligamenti su održanog kontinuiteta. 
Održan kontinuitet iliotibijalnog trakta, tetive muskulusa biceps femoris i tetive muskulusa popliteusa.
Primjeren je prikaz tetiva pes anserinus.
Vidljiv je izljev u u burzi m. semimembranozusa, posteromedijalno kaudalno uz vidljivu manju poplitealnu cistu promjera 11 mm.
Distenzija medijalnog patelarnog retinakuluma.
Tendinopatija tetive m. kvadriceps femoris.
Održan je ligament patele, smanjene napetosti, moguće hiperekstenzijski položaj pri snimanju.
Ne nalazi se signifikantnog izljeva u koljenskom zglobu.

Артикулиращия хрущял на фемура и тибията от медиалната страна е изтънен, стеснена е медиалната ставна междина с наличие на „вакуум феномен“ в нея. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост. МР данни за увреда на медиалния менискус. Менискусът се представя с дифузно повишен интензитет на сигнала на фона на стеснената ставна междина. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Нормално изобразяване на колатералните лигаменти. Хрущял на пателата, ретинакулуми – без особености. Лигамент на пателата и сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – б.о. Поплитеална ямка – нормално изобразяване. Заключение: МР данни за гонартроза, по-изразена от медиалната страна на колянната става – 2 към 3 степен по класификацията на Kellgren and Lawrence. Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales continuos.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservados, sin criterios de rotura. Pequeño ganglión intraóseo
de 7 mm adyacente a la raíz anterior del menisco medial.
Cartílago femorotibial con alteración de señal y discreta regularidad superficial, sin defectos
condrales profundos.
Cartílago rotuliano con alteración de señal y defectos de espesor parcial y subtotal, algunos
delaminativos, en ambas vertientes y vértice la patela destacando una úlcera profunda con
cambios óseos reactivos en el vértice.
Cartílago troclear con discreta irregularidad superficial en la región central.
Tendones regionales de espesor y señal conservados.
No hay derrame articular. No se observa quiste de Baker. Edema del aspecto superolateral de la
grasa de Hoffa.
Planos musculares de trofismo y señal conservados.
Impresión:
Condropatía femorotibial superficial.
Condropatía rotuliana con focos grado 3 y 4.

Erhaltene Artikulation im rechten Kniegelenk. Deutliches Ödem in der medialen Femurkondyle sowie im medialen Tibiaplateau. Kleinzystische Veränderungen subcortikal an der Patellafacette (5/9). Ansonsten unauffälliges Knochenmarkssignal. Patella zentriert stehend.

Weitere tief greifende chondrale Läsion auch an der medialen Patellafacette mit chondraler Ossifikationen mit ca. 6 x 6 mm (4/14 und 7/18). An den Femurkondylen der facies patellaris oberflächliche Chondropathie mit ausgedünntem Knorpelbelag. Auch femorotibial, führend medialseitig multiple tief greifende kontralaterale Läsionen, exemplarisch in der Hauptbelastungszone mit bis zu 4 mm (5/22) oder dorsal an der medialen Femurkondyle (5/24). Am medialen Tibiaplateau zudem kleine osteochondrale Läsion (5/20). Auch lateralseitig führend am dorsalen Tibiaplateau vollschichtige Chondropathie mit darunterliegenden kleinzystischen Veränderungen (1006/82). Die Kreuzbänder intakt. Diskrete Signalanhebung im Außenmeniskushinterhorn und im Bereich der anterioren Anheftungsstelle (6/22), DD bei mukoider Degeneration. Das Innenmeniskushinterhorn ebenfalls deutlich T2 signalalteriert mit komplexer in erster Linie degenerativer Rissbildung im Hinterhorn bis in die Pars intermedia (siehe z. B. 5/22). OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Acute subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle. Confluent subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle. Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus. Superiorly displaced meniscal flap at the medial joint line and at the posterior horn. Severe meniscal extrusion.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small complex tear of the lateral meniscal body, characterized by a dominant horizontal component.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity at the weightbearing aspect of the joint without focal defect.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness chondral defect at the lateral patellar facet measuring 6 x 6 mm. Focal full-thickness fissuring at the patellar median ridge. Areas of full-thickness fissuring at the medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Chronic partial tearing at the femoral attachment of the fibular collateral ligament.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 15 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Intramuscular edema at the popliteus and tibialis anterior, possibly reflecting low-grade strains. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. Deep soft tissue edema at the posterior thigh. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the weightbearing medial femoral condyle without articular surface collapse. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. 
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion with synovitis.
3.	Complex degenerative tearing throughout the medial meniscus with multiple displaced meniscal flaps and severe meniscal extrusion.
4.	Complex tearing of the lateral meniscal body.
5.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, severe in the medial compartment.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear extending from the posterior root to body of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage fissuring along the posterior weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage edema on the lateral patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complex medial meniscus tear from posterior root to body. Moderate extrusion.
2.	Minimal patellofemoral and medial compartment chondrosis.
3.	Small knee effusion and small Baker's cyst.

Geringer medialer Reizzustand. LCL mit intakter Signalgebung. Mäßiger Kniegelenkserguss mit Reizsynovialitis. Ausgedehnte, lobulierte Baker-Zyste mit einer CC-Ausdehnung von 8,4 cm und einem einzelnen Chondrom (1014/45). Quadriceps- sowie Patellarsehne mit intakter Signalgebung. От латералната страна се виждат дефекти в ставния хрущял в блисост с интеркондиларните еминенции. Сравнително запазен е хрущяла на пателата. МР данни за мадсивни остеофити по кондилите на фемура и тибията. Сравително по-малки остеофити се изобразяват и в горния и долен край на пателата. Изострени са интеркондиларните еминенциии. Наличие на ставен излив. МР данни за руптура на предната кръстна връзка с давност. Задната кръстна връзка е интактна. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Визуализират се дегенеративни промени в двата менискуса – при латералния менискус в областта на предния рог, докато медиалният менискус е дегенерирал изцяло. Задният рог на  медиалния менискус е фрагментиран. Наличие на слабо изразен субхондрален костномозъчен едем във фемура и тибията от медиалната страна. Фрагментиран е  задния рог на медиалния менискус. Рутура на предната кръстна връзка. Ставен излив. Бекерова киста. Дясна колянна става:При дясната колянна става също се установяват напреднали дегенеративни промени, предимно от медиалната страна. Нарушена е конгруентността на ставата, като ставата е сублуксирана. Ставният хрущял от медиалната страна страна е лизиран изцяло. Фрагментирален и зедният рог на медиалния менискус, като част от менискуса липсва. Силно дегенерирал е предният рог на медиалния менискус. Предният рог на менискуса е уголемен и с повишен интензитет на сигнала. Вижда е се и киста, сквързана с предния рог на медиалния менискус. Лателарният менискус е сравнително запазен. Ставният хрущял от латералната страна е с неравности в контурните очертания, съответстващи на локални дефекти. МР днни за остеофити по ставните краища на фемура и тибията. Изострени са интеркондиларните еминенции. Кръстните връзки са интактни. Визуализира се изрезен субхондрален костно-мозъчен едем в тибията. Вижда се чуждо тяло /ставна мишка/ в ставата. Чуждото тяло е с кръгла форма и големина 7мм, локализирано е дорзално, до ставната капсула и медиално. Голям ставен излив. Заключение: МР данни за напреднала гонартроза, по-изразена от медиалната страна на дясната колянна става. Дегенеративна промяна и руптура на медиалния менискус. Сублуксация на дясната колянна става. Чуждо тяло /ставна мишка/ в дясната колянна става. Ставен излив.

Findings:  Large joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments. Prominent bursa deep to the MCL.  Complex degenerate tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a full-thickness radial component of the body and a superiorly displaced component adjacent to the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle (see image snap shot). Intact lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band and pes anserine tendons. Small ganglion around the popliteus tendon.  Intact extensor mechanism. No evidence of fat pad impingement.  High-grade chondral thinning in the weightbearing portion of the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Focal high-grade chondropathy in the lateral tibial condyle with minor underlying bone stress change. High-grade chondral thinning and full-thickness chondral loss across the majority of the medial and lateral retropatellar facets. Full-thickness chondral loss is also noted in the lateral aspect of the lateral femoral trochlea groove with underlying bone stress change.  
Conclusion:  Large knee joint effusion. Complex tear of the medial meniscus as described above. MCL bursa. Tricompartmental degenerative change, prominent in the patellofemoral compartment. Ancillary findings described above.

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Progressive right knee pain in the region of the medial meniscus, suspected medial meniscal tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Result cleavage tear extends through the posterior horn of the medial meniscus into the body, without medial meniscal extrusion. Multilobulated meniscal cyst adjacent to the posterior horn, measuring 9 x 5 x 4 mm. The posterior root is intact. The anterior horn is intact.

The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments are intact. Iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Mild patellofemoral chondrosis. Mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis. The lateral femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. No erosions or periostitis. No synovitis or tenosynovitis.

IMPRESSION:
1. Horizontal cleavage tear posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus though medial meniscal extrusion. Parameniscal cyst formation adjacent to the posterior horn.
2. Nonspecific chondrosis medial and patellofemoral compartments, compatible with mild osteoarthritis most pronounced involving the medial femorotibial compartment. No specific imaging features of inflammatory arthritis.

Clinical information: Left knee pain for 8 weeks, atraumatic. No improvement with physiotherapy/rehabilitation. Positive meniscus tests. Concern for LCL tear versus lateral meniscal tear. Rule out internal derangement of the knee.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
There is a radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus measuring 4.5 x 3.5 mm. There is an fraying of the residual posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There are no displaced meniscal fragments. There is a moderate mucoid degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no acute tear of the lateral meniscus.

The cruciate ligaments are intact. There is a moderate thickening with associated T2 hyperintensity of the proximal medial collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial and lateral femorotibial joint compartment. 

There is an mild chondrosis at the medial and lateral patellar facet with focal superficial cartilage irregularities at the lateral patellar facet. There are no cartilage defects, no subchondral bone marrow edema.

There is no joint effusion. There is no Baker's cyst. 

The joint articulations are well-maintained. 

There is a lobulated ganglion cyst extending along the popliteus tendon measuring 4.5 x 1.4 cm in the axial plane.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. The visualized muscle bulk is intact.

Conclusion:
1. Radial tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. No displaced meniscal fragments. 
2. No acute ligamentous injury, especially no tear of the lateral collateral ligament.
3. Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

Interprétation :

Minime épanchement intra-articulaire. Liséré de liquide au sein du récessus poplité sans kyste de Baker significatif. 

Le ménisque interne et le ligament collatéral interne sont intacts sans déchirure.

Légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne sans atteinte transfixiante, en lien avec de légers changements dégénératifs/chondropathie. Ébauche d’ostéophytes marginaux.

Le ménisque externe de même que le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts sans déchirure. Les surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe sont relativement préservées sans atteinte transfixiante.

Il y a une infiltration kystique ganglionnaire au sein du ligament croisé antérieur sans déchirure transfixiante. Également, petits kystes para-ligamentaires. Le ligament croisé postérieur est intact sans déchirure.

Il y a une patella alta. Il y a un foyer d’œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa en lien avec un syndrome de friction du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe. Légère tendinose du tendon patellaire sans déchirure.  Légère tendinose du tendon du quadriceps distal, sans déchirure.

Il y a une atténuation modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment patellofémoral avec fissures chondrales de haut grade le long de la facette patellaire externe et de l’apex patellaire en lien avec des changements dégénératifs/chondropathie modérée. De plus, foyer de chondropathie focale sévère à la facette patellaire interne avec fissures chondrales transfixiantes et petit foyer de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ébauche d’ostéophytes marginaux.

Conclusion :

Il n’y a pas de dérangement interne (pas de déchirure méniscale ou ligamentaire significative).

Patella alta. Signes d’un syndrome d’accrochage du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe (Hoffa’s fat pad impingement).

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament are intact and unremarkable. The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is no significant Baker's cyst.

Normal marrow signal.

No evidence of a significant knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION: 

No evidence of internal derangement.

Stable findings since previous MRI.

Degenerative maceration is noted throughout the posterior half of the medial meniscus, with medial extrusion at the level of the body, together with a small inferiorly displaced fragment that is best appreciated in the coronal plane. There is resultant bowing of an otherwise intact superficial MCL.  An undisplaced tear through the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is also present, along with mucoid degeneration at the corresponding anterior horn.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus, distal iliotibial band and the extensor tendons. No fracture or marrow infiltration.  Reasonably well-maintained lateral weightbearing and patellofemoral articular cartilage surfaces, diffuse grade 2 thinning of medial weightbearing articular cartilage noted. Focal subcortical cystic change noted at the tibial aspect of the medial tibiofemoral joint line, presumed reactive in nature given the overlying extensive degenerative maceration.  Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There are foci of bone marrow edema at the terminal sulcus of the lateral femoral condyle and posterior lateral tibial plateau consistent with a recent pivot shift type injury. No suspicious bone marrow signal abnormality is identified.

Alignment is anatomic. There is a small to moderate knee joint effusion. No calcified/ossified intra-articular bodies are identified. Trace Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Small focus of surfacing signal abnormality (seen best on series 4, image 21 and series 6, image 19), which may represent a small undersurface tear at the junction of the body/posterior horn of the medial meniscus. No extrusion, displaced fragment, or para meniscal cyst is identified.

Lateral meniscus: Intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Markedly edematous and enlarged with near complete/complete mid substance disruption.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact; minimal periligamentous edema could indicate a grade 1 sprain. A tiny amount of fluid interposed between the intermediate and deep layers could represents trace MCL bursitis.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex/posterolateral corner structures: Intact; periligamentous edema about the fibular collateral ligament and popliteofibular ligaments without significant fiber disruption compatible with grade 1 sprains.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

Small amount of intramuscular edema/fluid noted within the proximal muscle belly of the soleus compatible with a grade 2 strain. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

2. Suspected small undersurface tear at the junction of the body/posterior horn of the medial meniscus, as described.

3. Grade 2 strain of the proximal soleus muscle.

4. Minimal medial/lateral compartment chondrosis.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Fall onto left knee while downhill skiing 3 months ago. Immediate bruising. Has had residual swelling and medial joint line pain. X-ray is negative for OA. Please evaluate for meniscal or ligamentous pathology.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Radial tear posterior horn and adjacent posterior root of the medial meniscus with slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

ACL, PCL MCL and LCL are intact.

MCL and LCL are intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.

Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament. No patellofemoral subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits.

Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture peripheral weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle, measuring 8 mm anterior to posterior and 6 mm medial to lateral. Exuberant surrounding marrow edema. No evidence of displaced 1 stable osteochondral fragment.

Focal fissuring of articular cartilage central weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle as well as central to medial femoral trochlea and along the patellar apex and medial patellar facet.

Incidental finding 0.8 x 1.1 x 1.3 cm lowT1 signal intensity and high T2 signal intensity lesion, likely to represent an enchondroma.

3.5 x 1.3 x 2.7 cm the Baker's cyst. Trace fluid in the pes anserine bursa.

Small volume joint effusion.

INTERPRETATION:

1. Radial tear posterior root and posterior horn of the medial meniscus slight extrusion. 
2. Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema.
3. Medial femorotibial and patellofemoral chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral compartment suggesting evolving mild patellofemoral predominant osteoarthritis of the left knee. 
4. Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament without patellofemoral subluxation. 
5. Mild pes anserine bursitis.
6. Incidental finding of enchondroma.

JOINT EFFUSION:  Small joint effusion. Small leaking popliteal cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  Subchondral fracture line is noted along the weightbearing segment of the medial femoral condyle, with probable nondisplaced osteochondral lesion. This measures 15 mm AP and 10 mm transverse. Moderate degree of associated bone marrow edema.

There is also mild medial compartment osteoarthritis, with subchondral cystic changes of the tibial plateau. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Low-grade fissuring of the patellar cartilage. No high-grade or full-thickness cartilage defect. No subchondral edema. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Superior and inferior patellar enthesophytes. Small interstitial tear in the proximal patellar tendon. 

BONE MARROW:  As above. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Large horizontal undersurface tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Mild peripheral meniscal extrusion.

2. Subchondral fracture line of the medial femoral condyle, likely in the context of nondisplaced osteochondral lesion.

3. Mild medial compartment osteoarthritis.

4. Grade 1 sprain pattern of the medial collateral ligament. Intact cruciate ligaments.

5. Small knee joint effusion and leaking popliteal cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: One month of knee pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Focal subchondral marrow edema at the anterior peripheral margin of the medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: High-grade radial tear of the posterior root with moderate peripheral extrusion and superimposed complex tearing of the body and posterior horn.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large areas of full-thickness chondrosis along the weightbearing femoral condyle with underlying subchondral cystic change/edema. Diffuse high-grade tibial cartilage loss with full-thickness loss at the peripheral margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the femoral condyle and tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss along the superior aspect of the medial patellar facet with underlying subchondral cystic change and edema. Diffuse thinning of the trochlear cartilage, without focal defect.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact, with thickening of the proximal ligament suggestive of prior injury. Bowed morphology and periligamentous edema likely secondary to meniscal extrusion.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Moderate to severe medial compartment osteoarthritis with complex meniscal tearing and reactive subchondral edema at the peripheral medial tibial plateau.

CLINICAL HISTORY:One-year history of right knee pain with instability.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Complex tear posterior horn medial meniscus consistent with a focal radial tear as well as inferiorly surfacing oblique tear, the latter extending into the medial meniscal body which is slightly peripherally extruded. The posterior root is intact. The anterior horn is intact.

The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal tibial mid fibers of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Components of the deep medial collateral ligament including the posterior oblique ligament are intact.

The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Minimal lateral patellar subluxation. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 16 mm, above the upper limit of normal. The patellar retinacula are intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Mild patellofemoral chondrosis. Mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis with subtle cartilage thinning. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tear posterior horn medial meniscus with slight medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Mild to moderate tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment suggesting evolving mild osteoarthritis of the right knee.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Component of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact.
4. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.
5. Lateralization of the tibial tubercle, which may predispose to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. At most minimal lateral patellar subluxation.

COMPARISON:[Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:One-year history right knee pain after blunt trauma to the anterior knee.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. Minimal lateral patellar subluxation. There is edema within the superolateral aspect of the infrapatellar fat-pad, suggesting underlying lateral femoral condylar patellar tendon friction syndrome. This is new from previous study. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits.

There is mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis, new since previous study. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Progressive mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis suggesting evolving patellofemoral osteoarthritis.
2. Infrapatellar fat pad edema suggestive of underlying lateral femoral condylar patellar tendon friction syndrome.

Bones:
There is a tiny subchondral impaction fracture at the posterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with associated moderate bone marrow edema.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

1.There is a tiny subchondral impaction fracture at the posterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau.

Kleines Kontusionsödem am anteromedialen Femurcondylus (Serie 7/ Image 15). Ansonsten regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Radiärer Riss des Innenmeniskushinterhorns mit vertikaler Rissbildung in der Pars intermedia (Serie 3/ Image 112, Serie 7/ Image 22). Partialläsion des MCL bei angrenzend gering Flüssigkeit (Serie 7/ Image 18).

Laterales Kompartiment:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Intakter Außenmeniskus. Intaktes LCL. 

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Patella:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Bis nach subchondral reichender Knorpeldefekt der medialen Patellafacette (Outerbridge Grad 4) (Serie 3/ Image 56, Serie 8/ Image 27). Regelrechte Darstellung des Lig. patellae. Intakte Quadrizepssehne. Regelrechter Hoffa`scher Fettkörper.

Kreuzbänder:
Intakte Kreuzbänder. Mehrere, unspezifische kleine Zysten am Ansatz des HKB im posterioren Tibiaplateau (Serie 9/ Image 17).

Muskulatur und übrige Weichteile:
Geringer Gelenkerguss. Kleine Bakerzyste. Diffuse Flüssigkeitsstraßen im subkutanen Fettgewebe dorsolateral des distalen Femurschafts. Regelrechtes flow void in den miterfassten Gefäßen.

ligamenta promjene intenziteta signala koje mogu odgovarati kalcifikatima. Ne nalazi se jasnih
znakova rupture.
Stražnji križni ligament je blaže degenerativno promijenjen, održanog kontinuiteta.
Stanje po kompleksnoj rupturi medijalnog meniska na bazi degenerativnih promjena, vidljiva je
ekstruzija tijela meniska van koštanog okvira zgloba. Ruptura zahvaća stražnji korijen meniska.
Uz interkondilarnu eminenciju nalazi se "flap" meniska.
Lateralni menisk umjereno degenerativno promijenjen, bez jasne rupture.
Vanjski sloj medijalnog kolateralnog ligamenta održan. Promijenjen intenzitet signala
femoromeniscealnog i tibiomeniscealnog ligamenta, moguće stanje po rupturi.

promjene.

na femoralnom hvatištu i blaži burzitis tetive. Vidljiva je i ganglion cista na tetivno-mišićnom

Nalaze se degenerativne promjene hvatišta medijalne i lateralne glave muskulusa
gastroknemijusa za femur uz brojne sitne ganglion ciste.
Održani iliotibijalni trakt. Primjeren prikaz tetiva pes anserinus. Održana tetiva bicepsa.
Entezopatske promjene tetive kvadricepsa. Održan ligament patele.

zglobu.

Lateral meniscus: No tear.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with right knee pain to the lateral joint line and infrapatellar pain after injury. Rule out meniscal tear.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact. There is prepatellar edema which may correlate clinically with prepatellar bursitis.

 The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.4 consistent with mild patella alta. There is some attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum with slight lateral subluxation of the patella. Findings may relate to remote injury related to transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

There is chondral fissuring and chondral loss seen to the patellar apex and lateral facet associated with subcortical cyst formation in the patella and with edema. The articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea demonstrates mild chondral fissuring seen at the trochlear apex but is otherwise reasonably well-maintained. The TT TG distance measures about 9 mm, within normal limits.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus contains some mild non-surfacing signal in the posterior horn and body but demonstrates no surfacing meniscal tear.

The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is reasonably well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a multiloculated ganglion cyst seen within the popliteal fossa posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament. This measures 2.9 cm in height, and 1.1 by 0.8 cm in short axis. It is situated anterior to the lateral fibers of the medial head of the gastrocnemius.

There is no significant Baker's cyst. There is no evidence of significant knee effusion.

Marrow signal is otherwise within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Patella alta.

Severe chondromalacia patella. Associated attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum, possibly related to remote transient lateral patellar dislocation.

Prepatellar bursitis.

Popliteal fossa ganglion cyst as described.

No evidence of internal derangement.

Trouvailles :

Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire sans kyste poplité significatif.

Il y a des changements dégénératifs légers à modérés impliquant les trois compartiments plus proéminents impliquant le compartiment interne où il y a amincissement modéré du cartilage au condyle fémoral interne et au plafond tibial. Il y a léger amincissement du cartilage impliquant le compartiment externe.

Au niveau patellofémoral, il y a amincissement modéré à la partie centrale et médiale de la trochlée du fémur.

Il y a changements dégénératifs intra-substance impliquant le ménisque interne. Il y a une déchirure complexe multidirectionnelle impliquant le corps et la corne postérieure. Il y a une composante horizontale s’étendant de la corne postérieure jusqu’au niveau du corps. Il y a un fragment déplacé du ménisque en provenance de la corne postérieure déplacée antérieure à la racine postérieure. Il y a aussi un fragment déplacé au niveau du corps du ménisque avec extrusion. Le ménisque externe démontre des changements dégénératifs intra-substance sans déchirure linéaire bien définie.

Autrement le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et tendon du poplité, le biceps fémoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité.

Conclusion :

1. Légers changements dégénératifs plus proéminents au niveau du compartiment interne.

2. Progression de la déchirure méniscale du ménisque interne avec une déchirure complexe multidirectionnelle avec multiples fragments déplacés (composante de type FLAP) tel que détaillé ci-haut.

3. Petit épanchement intra-articulaire sans kyste poplité.

MRI of right Knee with

* Status of horizental tear of medial meniscus post arthroscopic repair for meniscus with FASTFIX*2 and microfracture for medial femur condyle on [DATE]
  Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, R/O re-tear; post-operative change.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> The contour of ACL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S PD, in favor of grade 1 injury.
  Mild interstitial increased signal intensity of MCL, in favor of grade 1 injury.
> The contour of PCL and LCL  within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> A small lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Fraying of articular cartilage of patella and femoral condyle, reflecting grade 3 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint.
    Osteophytes of right knee.
> Mild muscle edema over lateral head of gastrocnemius muscle.

1. C/W Re-tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus; differential diagnosis of post-operative change.
2. Osteoarthritis of right knee joint, more prominent atmedial compartment with grade 3 chondromalacia.
3. Mild synovitis and patellar plicae of right knee and small Baker's cyst .
4. Grade 1 injury of ACL and MCL.
5. Mild muscle edema over lateral head of gastrocnemius muscle.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is fissuring of articular cartilage at the central femoral trochlea with focal full thickness cartilage denuding along the medial patellar facet. No evidence of displaced or unstable osteochondral fragment. Femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Focal high-grade patellofemoral chondrosis as detailed above. No evidence of displaced or unstable osteochondral fragment.
2. No evidence of discrete meniscal, ligament, or tendon tear.

FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament near its femoral insertion. There are pivot shift bone marrow contusion with a subchondral impaction fracture involving the lateral femoral condyle with associated significant bone marrow edema. There are also bone contusion involving the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau without fracture.

There is high-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament with complete disruption of its fibers at its femoral attachment with also thickening and increased signal throughout the superficial component. There is no distal avulsion or proximal retraction of the distal superficial component. There is also complete tear of the deep meniscal femoral component with significant thickening of the meniscal tibial component.

There is a horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface. There is no displaced meniscal fragment. There is a an oblique tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus at the insertion of the Wrisberg ligament compatible with a Wrisberg rip.

There is edema involving the myotendinous junction of the popliteus. The popliteus tendon itself is intact.

Otherwise the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the semimembranosus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL.

2. High-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament without evidence of pseudocyst Stener.

3. Medial and lateral meniscal tear without displaced fragment.

4. Pivot shift bone marrow contusion with subchondral impaction fracture of the lateral femoral condyle.

5. Moderate knee joint effusion.
