Interprétation:

Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire avec signes de synovite chronique. Il y a un également un kyste de Baker associé à une prolifération synoviale/synovite chronique s'étendant sur environ 5 cm de diamètre cc. Celui-ci s'étend au niveau des bourses du semi-membraneux et de la patte d'oie avec composante de bursite probablement associée. 

Il y a une déchirure complexe du ménisque interne avec déchirure radiaire transfixiante à la jonction de la racine postérieure et de la corne postérieure, et déchirure longitudinale horizontale impliquant la corne postérieure résiduelle, corps méniscal et s'étendant à la jonction avec la corne antérieure. Il y a une extrusion marquée du corps méniscal de façon associée. De plus, il y a une structure légèrement hétérogène et principalement hypointense ovalaire située de façon intime avec le rebord postérieur de la racine postérieure du ménisque interne mesurant 7 x 14 x 7 mm. L'aspect est plutôt en faveur d'une souris intra-articulaire qui pourrait être en partie ossifiée versus un ossicule méniscal (moins probable). L'aspect est moins en faveur d'un ''flap'' méniscal dont le signal demeure légèrement différent du ménisque et sans continuité démontrée avec la corne postérieure. 

Le ligament collatéral interne est intact sans déchirure. Il y a une atténuation modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne avec atteinte transfixiante aux surfaces portantes et petits ostéophytes marginaux. Pas de changement sous-chondral réactionnel associé. 

Le ménisque externe de même que le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts sans déchirure. 

Légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe, plus marquée à la surface portante. Petits ostéophytes marginaux.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. Petit kyste ganglionnaire para-ligamentaire.

L'alignement patello-fémoral est préservé. Le tendon du quadriceps distal est intact sans déchirure. Légère tendinose du patellaire sans déchirure. 

Atténuation modérée des surfaces chondrales au compartiment patello-fémoral avec fissure chondrale partielle le long de la surface articulaire patellaire et atteinte transfixiante le long de la surface trochléaire. Pas de changement sous-chondral réactionnel associé. Petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Conclusion:

Déchirure complexe du ménisque interne avec composante radiaire transfixiante à la jonction de la corne postérieure et de la racine postérieure avec extrusion significative du corps méniscal secondairement, de plus, déchirure longitudinale horizontale de la corne postérieure résiduelle et du corps du ménisque interne s'étendant à la jonction avec la corne antérieure.

Changements dégénératifs/chondropathie tricompartimentaux de grade 3 impliquant les compartiments fémoro-tibiaux interne et patello-fémoral et de grade 1 impliquant le compartiment fémoro-tibial externe.

Indication: Left knee pain for 2 weeks. No known cause.

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Large T1/T2 hypointense, cortically based lesion along the distal medial femoral diaphysis with a slightly broader zone of transition in expected, likely represents an old nonossifying fibroma.

JOINT SPACE:
Large joint effusion with increased T1 signal compatible with hemarthrosis, with extensive synovial proliferation, including more focal focal synovitis at the posterosuperior joint space. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage thinning, heterogeneity, and fissuring along weightbearing medial femoral condyle tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the medial patellar facet with focal high grade fissuring.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

original_report:
Erhaltene Artikulation am linken Kniegelenk. Geringes subchondrales Knochenödem am medialen femorotibialen Kompartiment (5/23). Stigmata der Osteopenie. Ansonsten unauffälliges Knochenmarksignal. Osteophytäre Anbauten am oberen und unteren Patellapol (6/22) sowie am medialen femorotibialen Gelenkspalt und geringer auch am lateralen Gelenkspalt (z. B. 5/18).
Patella zentriert stehend. Femoralseitig an der Trochlea mittig und am Übergang zur medialen Kondyle fokal auch tiefgreifende Chondropathie mit einzelnen chondralen Osteophyten (zB 3/66). Geringe oberflächliche Chondropathie medialseitig retropatellar (4/14). Femorotibial medialseitig in der Hauptbelastungszone großflächig  vollständig aufgebrauchte Knorpelschicht (z. B. 5/19), geringe Abflachung der Konvexität der Femurkondyle und subchondraler Sklerosierung (6/10). Lateralseitig geringe oberflächliche Chondropathie ohne tief greifende Chondropathie bei noch erhaltenem Knorpelbelag.
Der Innenmeniskus deutlich exkludiert und in der Pars intermedia signalangehoben mit degenerativem Horizontalriss in der pars intermedia und Hinterhorn (zB 5/22). Der Außenmeniskus morphologisch unauffällig ohne abnorme T2 Signalanhebung. Vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband durchgehend abgrenzbar jedoch T2 signalangehoben. Kollateralbänder ebenfalls intakt. Geringer Gelenkerguss. Plica mediopatellaris (4/11). Synovia verdickt. Umgebende Muskulatur und Subkutis unauffällig.

Na seriji MR presjeka desnog koljena nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala lateralnog
kolateralnog ligamenta, stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarne tetive i
tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Kompleksna degenerativna ruptura korpusa i stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska. Korpus meniska
periferno je potisnut izvan zglobne pukotine.
Lateralni menisk blaže deg. promijenjen, oblikovan po tipu diskoidnog meniska.
Blaže deg. promjene prednjeg križnog ligamenta.
Reaktivni periligamentarni edem medijalnog kolateralnog ligamenta.
Gotovo potpuni gubitak hrskavice medijalnog kodnila femura i tibije s edemom podliježeće
subhondralne kosti (hondromalacija 3. stupnja prema ICRS klasifikaciji).
Hrskavica obje fasete patele, trohleje femura i laterlanog kodnila femura i tibije prožeta je
fisurama i defektima pune debljine hrskavice (hondromalacija 3. stupnja prema ICRS
klasifikaciji).
Rubna osteofitoza zglobnih tijela.
Opsežan izljev u koljenu. Ne nalazi se poplitealne (Bakerove) ciste.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.

Na učinjenim MR presjecima kroz lijevo koljeno vidljiva kompletna ruptura prednjeg križnog
ligamenta u srednjoj trećini uz parcijalnu rupturu vlakana prednjeg korijena lateralnog meniska.
Vidljiva horizontalna ruptura stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska koji je degenerativno
promijenjen, uz znakove parcijalne meniskokapsularne separacije stražnjeg roga meniska od
posteriorne čahure koja je distendirana. Opisano odgovara ramp leziji.
Nalazi se manja zona koštanog edema medijalnog tibijalnog platoa te manje subkortikalne ciste
u području interkondilarne eminencije na hvatištu prednjeg križnog ligamenta.
Vidljive su fisure kondilarne i tibijalne hrskavice u smislu hondromalacije II. stupnja.
Areali hondromalacije I. stupnja trohlearne i patelarne hrskavice.
Stražnji križni ligament održan.
Bez znakova rupture lateralnog meniska.
Održan je kontinuitet kolateralnih ligamenata koljena uz znakove blaže distenzije medijalnog
kolateralnog ligamenta.
Vidljivo je raslojavanje vlakana proksimalnog dijela tetive muskulusa popliteusa, moguća manja
parcijalna ruptura.
Distenzija tetive m. semimembranozus uz uz manji izljev u burzi mišića. Ne nalazi se formirane
poplitealne ciste.
Primjeren je prikaz tetive m. kvadriceps i ligamenta patele.
Manja količina zglobnog izljeva.
Ostale strukture u granicama normale.

Right knee MRI:

INDICATION: Right knee [Age] female with remote history of right meniscal tearing seen for subacute, traumatic bilateral medial knee pain right more than left.? Degenerative.

COMPARISON: No prior images available at time of interpretation.

FINDINGS:

Mild knee joint effusion. Tiny 2.7 x 1.8 x 0.6 cm Baker's cysts.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Overall moderate to severe chondrosis more prominent on the medial facet of the patella. No significant subchondral marrow edema but full-thickness cartilage denuding. Extensor mechanism is intact. Hoffa's fat pads unremarkable.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Moderate chondrosis. Small osteophytes. There is macerated posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with multidirectional tearing extension to the meniscal undersurface with slightly medially extruded meniscus, no flipped fragment or free fragment identified. 2.3 x 1.2 x 0.8 cm posterior parameniscal cyst. Medial collateral ligament and pes anserine tendons are intact. Mild semimembranosus tendinosis.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Mild chondrosis with minimal thinning. No subchondral bone change. Tiny osteophytes. Minimal heterogeneous signal to the posterior horn of the meniscus without discrete tear related to chronic degeneration. Lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris tendons are intact. Popliteus tendon is intact. The iliotibial band is unremarkable.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligament are intact. Effusion/ganglion cyst extending into the posterior intercondylar notch.

IMPRESSION:
1. Moderate to severe chondrosis of the femoral patellar compartment, moderate chondrosis of the medial femoral tibial compartment and mild chondrosis of the lateral compartment. Degenerative changes associated with mild knee joint effusion.
2. Complex multidirectional degenerative tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild meniscal extrusion but no flipped or free fragment. Associated parameniscal cyst.

COMPARISON:[Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right lateral knee pain, chronic. Suspected lateral meniscal tear/lateral collateral ligament tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. Horizontal cleavage tear with superior surfacing noted extending through the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is an additional radial tear involving the lateral meniscal body. The latter is unchanged from <[YEAR]>. The former is new since previous study. No lateral meniscal extrusion. The posterior root and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus are intact. Possible additional inferiorly subtle tear at the periphery of the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus, also new since previous study.

The anterior cruciate ligament and T2 are intact. Medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. Fibular collateral ligament is intact. Popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments are intact. Iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. There is mild lateral patellar subluxation, similar to previous. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 13 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Focal soft tissue articular cartilage central femoral trochlea, also seen present. Mild chondrosis throughout the remainder the patellofemoral compartment. Mild medial and lateral femorotibial chondrosis, slightly progressed when compared to previous. Probable insertional cyst near the anterior cruciate ligament footplate. 

Prominent red marrow, similar to previous. Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:
1. Interval development of horizontal cleavage tear extending through the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus without lateral meniscal extrusion. Unchanged radial tear involving the lateral meniscal body. Possible additional inferiorly surfacing oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus.
2. Mild to moderate chondrosis has progressed slightly since previous study, and is compatible with evolving mild osteoarthritis of the right knee.

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture . Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Mild marrow edema along the lateral cortex along the tibial plateau, may represent a small osseous contusion.

Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

Rotura compleja del menisco medial con segmento que se insinúa hacia el receso menisco femoral

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right-sided knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, consistent with extensive complex tearing. The anterior horn shows intrasubstance degeneration without tear. The posterior root is barely perceptible consistent with extensive complex tear. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body.

Barely perceptible posterior root of the lateral meniscus raising suspicion for complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. No lateral meniscal extrusion. 

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with intrasubstance ganglion formation. Slight anterior tibial translation.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament near the medial femoral condyle origin. The meniscotibial meniscal femoral component of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact. The posterior oblique ligament is intact.

Fibular collateral ligament is intact. Moderate popliteus tendinosis of the lateral femoral condylar attachment, without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 15 mm, at the upper limit of normal. No patellofemoral subluxation.

There is focal full thickness cartilage denuding at the patellar apex with fissuring of articular cartilage at the patellar apex and extending along the medial patellar facet. There is diffuse full-thickness cartilage denuding throughout the weightbearing aspect of the medial femorotibial compartment with subchondral sclerosis. There is mild to moderate lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Prominent non-marginal lateral femoral condylar osteophyte.

Trace knee joint fluid. Subcutaneous edema along the lateral and posterior aspects of the knee and proximal calf. There is generalized atrophy of the regional musculature which maybe on the basis of deconditioning. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Extensive complex tear involving the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion and tricompartment chondrosis as pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment, consistent with severe medial compartment predominant tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.
2. Suspected complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus without lateral meniscal extrusion.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament. Components of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact.
4. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
5. Borderline lateralization of the tibial tubercle which may predispose to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. No patellofemoral subluxation.
6. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with slight anterior tibial translation.

original_report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.16 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is intense bone marrow edema within the medial femoral condyle with a subchondral crescent of low signal at the central weightbearing aspect, consistent with a subchondral insufficiency fracture. There is no significant articular surface collapse. No evidence of osteonecrosis. Mild degenerative subchondral cystic change is present at the inferior patella. Background bone marrow signal is otherwise normal. 

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a large radial tear at the posterior root attachment. Moderate extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild to moderate cartilage thinning/fissuring diffusely.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is fraying of the inner margin along the body and posterior horn. Small tear at the posterior root attachment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is moderate to severe cartilage loss at the patella and trochlea, with mild subchondral cystic change.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact, with surrounding edema compatible with hyperemia related to adjacent medial compartment disease.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Diffuse periarticular soft tissue edema, most prominent medially.

IMPRESSION:

1. Subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.
2. Tear at the posterior root attachment of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion. Small tear of the lateral meniscus.
3. Chondrosis in the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

-3-Plane Loc, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, AX GRE T2*, Cor T2 FS, Screen Save

> Status of hemophilia B according to history
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with intermediate to mild hypointensity signal  on T1WI and heterogenous hyperintenisty signal inside, but no significant fluid-fluid interface,  C/W chronic hemarthrosis; suprapatellar and medial plicae.
    Irregular hypointensity signal material surround the joint capsule in left joint on all sequence, in favor of hypertrophy of the synovium with hemosiderin deposition ( especially at intercondylar region),  reflecting of hemophilic synovitis.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee and mild mild subchondral bone edema and cysts over distal femur and tibial plateua; in favorof some  bone erosions.
> Suspicious of linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with suspicious of extending into the surface, R/O tear. 
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 5 cm in length; [DATE] . Mild perifocal edema.
> Mild  subcutaneous edema over right knee and muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
> Subcutanoues edema and interstitial muscle edema over right proximal leg, more prominent in comparison with last MRI.
> Interstitial increased signal intensity of the muscles in left lower thigh, major at  anterior and posteror compartment of left lower thigh, including quadriceps muscles and biceps femoris muscle; in favor of intermusuclar hyperintensity area along biceps femoris muscle, maybe due to intermuscular edema/ hemorrhage .
    Minimal fluid accumulation in semimembranousus muscle and semitendinousus tendon
    
Impression: 
1. C/W hemophilic arthropathy of  left knee joint with prominent hemophilic synovitis and in favor of  chronic hemarthrosis and bulging of suprapatellar bursitis and Baker's cyst; patellar plicae.
2. [DATE]; in favor of some intermuscular edema/ hemorrahge along biceps femoris muscle.
3. R/O degeneration and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Mucoid degeneration of the ACL.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:

original_report:
MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    5 weeks ago patient felt popping sensation in the right knee during rotation motion. Able to weight-bear at the time of injury and presently tenderness at fibular head. Difficulty flexing the past 90 degrees. Ultrasound revealed effusion with synovial thickening and positive McMurray's test for medial aspect in clinic.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There are no normal intact fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament in keeping with a complete mid fiber tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The finding is associated with an anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment of about 8 mm. There is evidence of resolving bone contusions in the anterior lateral femoral condyle with slightly depressed anterior sulcus and resolving bone contusions in the posterior lateral tibial plateau. Findings are consistent with resolving kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is also edema in the posterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau.

Buckling of the posterior cruciate ligament is noted in association with the anterior tibial drawer. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

The medial collateral ligament is intact. There is some mild intrinsic signal around the deep fibers of the medial collateral ligament in keeping with a low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. Large intra-articular organized soft tissue hematoma measuring 5.2 x 1.5 x 5.8 cm.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with full-thickness tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild loss of substance of the posterior horn.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Complete avulsion of the biceps femoris from the fibular head associated with a large multiloculated soft tissue hematoma surrounding the tear extending along the lateral gastrocnemius muscle.
Complete avulsion of the popliteus tendon at its insertion on the lateral femoral condyle.
Severe edema and irregularity of the lateral collateral ligament proper with high-grade partial-thickness tear from its femoral attachment and complete avulsion from its fibular attachment.
No fracture of the fibular head is identified.

Longitudinal vertical tear of the peripheral posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus.
Diffuse chondral thinning without deep fissuring.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Avulsion of the posterior cruciate ligament from its femoral attachment.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Normal.

Bones:
Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Diffuse edema of the visualized proximal anterior compartment of the leg muscles. Associated diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.Sequela of knee dislocation with complete tears of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments.
2.Extensive injury of the posterolateral corner with complete avulsion of the lateral collateral ligament proper, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon as described above.
3.High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with complete tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
4.Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild substance loss of the posterior horn.
5.Longitudinal vertical peripheral tear of the posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus compatible with a Wrisberg rip.
6.Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.
7.Diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting low-grade traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection. Associated denervation edema of the visualized anterior muscle compartment of the proximal leg.
8.Moderate knee joint effusion with large intra-articular organized hematoma

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with trauma during ski accident 1.5 weeks ago with persistent pain, swelling and limited range of motion of left knee.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are identified. There is a borderline anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 5 mm. There are bone contusions seen at the lateral femoral sulcus in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau consistent with kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is a discrete region of linear low T1 signal along the posterior rim of the lateral tibial plateau which may indicate presence of an undisplaced lateral tibial plateau rim fracture.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

There is abnormal signal surrounding the medial collateral ligament at its origin along its course proximal to the medial joint line consistent with grade 2 sprain. There is significant disruption of the deep fibers with intact superficial fibers extending distally. The posterior oblique ligament appears intact. There is an associated partial thickness sprain of the femoral insertion of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is some subtle increased signal seen in the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament which could indicate presence of a low-grade sprain. The fibular collateral ligament, IT band, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is abnormal increased T2 signal seen in the periphery of the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body consistent with a meniscocapsular avulsion injury. No discrete surfacing meniscal tear is identified to the medial meniscus. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is unremarkable. As noted the medial patellofemoral ligament at its femoral insertion demonstrates a partial thickness sprain. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained apart from some mild fissuring seen to the trochlear articular cartilage at the apex and involving the medial facet. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION:
 
Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with bone contusions corresponding to a pivot shift mechanism of injury and with possible undisplaced posterior tibial plateau fracturing. Plain film correlation is recommended.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

Minime liséré de liquide au sein du récessus supra-patellaire sans épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Kyste de Baker multi-lobulé et allongé s’étendant jusqu’à 8cm de diamètre CC. Pas d’évidence de complication ou signe de rupture.

Légère anomalie de signal linéaire iso-intense d’allure horizontale longitudinale s’étendant de la corne postérieure au corps méniscal et impliquant la surface articulaire supérieure, suggérant une déchirure d’allure chronique. Minimes changements dégénératifs mucoïdes par ailleurs.

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Multifocal areas of subchondral edema along the lateral tibial plateau and femoral condyles.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Periligamentous edema about the lateral collateral ligament with intact fibers.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.  

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Edema of the popliteus muscle. No muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis as well as subchondral marrow edema along both tibial plateau and femoral condyles and edema of the posterolateral corner. Findings are concerning for early inflammatory arthritis, for which aspiration should be considered.

Clinical information: Left knee pain, refractory to opioids. Please assess for internal derangement.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
The cruciate ligaments are intact. There is mild thickening of the proximal medial collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. There is mild tendinosis of the distal quadriceps tendon. Otherwise extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a degenerative oblique tear at the posterior horn/posterior aspect body of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface (12-20). There are no unstable meniscal fragments. There is a mild mucoid degeneration of the lateral meniscus.

There is a mild chondrosis in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a moderate chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment with a focal button osteophyte at the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle measuring 0.8 x 0.5 x 0.3 cm. There is no adjacent bone marrow edema. There is a moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with focal cartilage fibrillation and deep cartilage defects at the lateral patellar facet. The joint indications are well-maintained.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. There is a mild joint effusion. There are no intra-articular bodies. 

There is a low volume Baker's cyst. There is a thickening with associated edematous changes involving the medial patellar plica (13-10)

The visualized muscle bulk is unremarkable. There is mild thickening with associated T2 hyperintensity of the proximal popliteal tendon in keeping with a mild tendinosis.

Conclusion:
1. Degenerative oblique tear posterior horn/posterior aspect body of the medial meniscus.
2. No acute ligamentous injury.
3. Moderate chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment with a small button osteophyte.
4. Moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
5. Thickening with associated edematous changes of the medial patellar plica. This may be seen in medial patellar plica syndrome. Please correlate clinically.

Indication: Right knee pain for 2 weeks after rugby injury.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Severe osseous contusions at the medial and lateral femoral condyles and posterolateral and posteromedial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Complex tear of the posterior horn. No extrusion or displaced fragment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete midsubstance tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 sprain.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 1 sprain of the fibular collateral ligament. Normal distal iliotibial band, popliteus tendon, and biceps femoris tendon.
Posterolateral corner structures: Grade 1 soleus strain.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Recent pivot shift mechanism injury with complete ACL tear, pivot shift pattern osseous contusions, grade 1 sprain of the medial and fibular collateral ligaments, and grade 1 strain of the soleus.
2.	Complex tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.

FINDINGS: A partial injury of the anterior cruciate ligament is demonstrated - anatomical continuity is best appreciated in the coronal plane. There is in fact no associated anterior tibial translation.  Well-preserved medial and lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage surfaces, a subcentimeter focus of grade 3/4 articular cartilage loss is noted at the midline femoral trochlea anteriorly. Well-preserved retropatellar articular cartilage.  There is a significant, incompletely imaged knee joint effusion with nonspecific synovitis, no intra-articular loose bodies are present.  There is a popliteus muscle strain posteriorly, there is however no disruption of the corresponding musculotendinous unit or tendon.  The popliteofibular ligament appears sprained, there is furthermore soft tissue edema like signal change at the position of the arcuate ligament complex, suggestive of a sprain pattern - both limbs of the arcuate ligament can however be appreciated on coronal images (series 301 image 26), implying gross structural continuity.  Both collateral ligaments appear intact, as do the PCL, medial meniscus, patellar tendon, distal iliotibial band and marrow signal characteristics.  A tiny cleft is affecting the free edge of the lateral meniscus, at the junction between the body and anterior horn. Minor non calcific distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis also present. No other finding of note.   
</IMPRESSION/> Partial ACL injury with involvement of the popliteus muscle, popliteofibular and arcuate ligaments posterolaterally. Subcentimeter diameter focus of full-thickness cartilage loss with associated reactive marrow changes noted at the midline femoral trochlea.

Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: lateral dislocation of left patella
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is currently anatomic. Acute osseous contusions at the inferomedial patella and anterior lateral femoral condyle, consistent with a recent transient lateral patellar dislocation. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small-to-moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness chondral fissuring along the lateral facet with underlying subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Complete rupture of the medial patellofemoral ligament at the femoral attachment site. High-grade tearing of the medial patellar retinaculum at the patellar attachment with possible thin avulsed cortical fragment (series 6 image 6).
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Poststenotic soft tissue edema along the anterior medial femoral condyle.

IMPRESSION:

МР находка: Наличие на малък ставен излив. Изобразяват се остеофити по латералните и медиалните ставни краища на тибията и фемура, по задната повърхност на медиалния кондил на тибията, по предната повърхност на латералния кондил на тибията, по кондилите на фемура отпред и в двата полюса на пателата. Изтънен е артикулиращият хрущял на пателата и фемура в латералната половина на феморопателарната става. Наличие на отграничена зона на костномозъчен едем в пателата от тази страна. Без МР данни за хондромалация на пателата. Субхондрално разположени костни кисти в латералния кондил на бедрената кост. Изобразява се вътреставно разположена лезия с овална форма и нисък сигнален интензитет в PD и PD SPAIR. Находката е с размер 5/3 мм и е зад залавното място на задната кръстна връзка за тибията. Около описаната находка има малко количество течност. МР данни за хиперинтензна лезия с хоризонтален ход в задния рог на латералния менискус, която се проследява в тялото и в участък от предния рог на менискуса. Мултилокуларна киста на латералния менискус.
МР данни за хиперинтензна лезия с кос ход в задния рог на медиалния менискус, която достига до края на менискуса, без видимо да е в контакт с артикулиращите повърхности на тибията и фемура. Нормално изобразяване на предния рог на медиалния мениксус. Кръстните връзки са интактни. Ретинакулуми на пателата, колатерални лигаменти – б.о. Сухожилие на m. quadriceps femoris и лигамент на patella – със запазена цялост и сигнален интензитет. Наличие на подкожен едем по преднолатералната повърхност на подбедрицата. Moderate suprapatellar joint effusion, communicating with a large non ruptured Baker's cyst measuring just under 7 cm in maximal dimension, there are no intra-articular bodies.  
There is an extensive degenerative tear throughout the body and part of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with consequent medial extrusion at the level of the body. A small superiorly displaced fragment is appreciated posteriorly, at the junction of the corresponding posterior horn and root. 
 There is adjacent distal insertional semimembranosus tendinopathy.  
Intact lateral meniscus, cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus, distal iliotibial band and the extensor tendons. No fracture or marrow infiltration.  Diffuse grade 3 articular cartilage thinning noted throughout the central third of the medial femoral condyle, but with no associated insufficiency type bony injury.  
Generally well-maintained remaining tricompartmental articular cartilage surfaces.  Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the left knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Two-week history of lateral knee pain in Marathon runner. X-ray negative. Please rule out lateral tibial plateau stress reaction.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. No retinacular disruption. No trochlear dysplasia. The tibial tuberosity to trochlear groove distance is 13 mm, within normal limits. The patellofemoral cartilage is intact.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament are intact.

The medial and lateral menisci are intact. Mild chondrosis of the lateral tibiofemoral cartilage. The medial tibiofemoral cartilage is maintained.

The medial collateral ligament is intact. The fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band are intact. There is mild soft tissue edema deep to the distal fibers of the iliotibial band.

No abnormal bone marrow edema. No acute fracture. No Baker's cyst. Trace joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION:

1. No evidence of fracture.
2. Soft tissue edema deep to the distal fibers of the iliotibial band, which may correlate with clinical features of iliotibial band syndrome. The iliotibial band itself is intact.
3. Mild chondrosis of the lateral tibiofemoral cartilage.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Significant left knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive posterior root and posterior horn of the medial meniscus consistent with complex tear. Displaced 6 x 6 x 6 mm meniscal fragment adjacent to the posterior root. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Intrasubstance degeneration of the anterior root of the lateral meniscus without discrete lateral meniscal tear.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament involving the posterior lateral bundle. The anteromedial bundle is intact. No tibial translation. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Low-grade partial-thickness tears of the superficial medial collateral ligament as well as deep medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament. Mild fluid accumulation within the pes anserine bursa.

Popliteus tendinosis without tear. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Attenuated appearance of the medial patellofemoral ligament suggestive of prior tear. Mild lateral patellar subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is generalized thinning of patellofemoral articular cartilage. There is mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis. There is a nondisplaced 10 x 5 mm subchondral insufficiency fracture involving the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex medial meniscal tear with medial meniscal extrusion and 6 mm displaced meniscal fragment noted adjacent to the posterior root.
2. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without tibial translation.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tears involving the superficial and deep fibers of the medial collateral ligament.
4. Mild pes anserine bursitis.
5. Suspected prior tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament with only mild lateral patellar subluxation.
6. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
7. Tricompartment chondrosis consistent with mild-to-moderate tricompartment osteoarthritis of the left knee.
8. Nondisplaced 10 x 5 mm subchondral fracture medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema.

Höhergradig geminderter Knorpelbesatz am proximalen Tibiaplateau mit fokal vollschichtige Chondropathie über eine Ausdehnung von 9 x 19 mm (a.p. x ml, 6/8 sowie 5/20); flächig vollschichtige Chondropathie auch an der medialen Femurkondyle nach medial hin. Keine höhergradige Chondropathie im lateralen Kompartiment. Retropatellar geminderter Knorpelbesatz mit betont an der medialen Trochleafacette höhergradiger Chondropathie ohne fokal vollschichtigen chondralen Defekt. Ausgeprägter Substanzdefekt des Innenmeniskus in der Pars intermedia und im Hinterhorn mit aufgefaserter Struktur sowie radiärem Defekt am Hinterhorn (5/25). Kein Anhalt für eine Rissbildung des Außenmeniskus. VKB sowie HKB intakt. Geringer medialer Reizzustand. LCL mit intakter Signalgebung. Kein Kniegelenkserguss. Kleine, gering flüssigkeitsgefüllte Baker-Zyste. Fabella. 2 Chondrome dorsal. Quadriceps- sowie Patellarsehne mit intakter Signalgebung. Unauffällige Signalgebung der übrigen miterfassten Weichteile in den vorliegenden Sequenzen.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Mild bone marrow edema and cystic changes are present at the tibial spines and at the lateral femoral condyle centrally bordering on the intercondylar notch.. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Mild, diffuse synovial proliferation. Moderate Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear involving the posterior horn and body, with a large radial tear at the posterior root attachment. Moderate extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and surface irregularity diffusely. Small osteophytes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is a complex tear involving the anterior and posterior root attachments. Fraying of the inner margin diffusely. No extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is mild cartilage thinning at the posterior aspect, with cartilage fissuring centrally near the intercondylar notch.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring at the patella, medial greater than lateral. Trochlear cartilage appears intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): There is mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, which otherwise appears intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Degenerated, intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 6 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:


1. Medial and lateral meniscal tear. Medial meniscal extrusion.

2. Tricompartmental chondrosis.

3. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament.

4. Small joint effusion with synovial proliferation. Moderate Baker cyst.
